## How To Use This Log

Every implementation PR must append an entry before it is considered complete.

Required evidence:

- branch name.
- worktree path.
- implementation workstream, if used.
- PR link.
- scope completed.
- files changed.
- tests added.
- commands run.
- E2E/visual/manual QA evidence.
- local agent CLI QA evidence.
- CodeRabbit status.
- subagent reviews.
- unresolved findings.
- security/privacy notes.
- performance notes.
- performance measurements and budget status.
- migration notes.
- follow-up deletion conditions.

Do not mark a PR complete with skipped critical E2E, unresolved P0/P1 findings,
missing CodeRabbit review, or unmeasured performance-sensitive changes. Only
non-critical documentation-only exceptions may be overridden by explicit user
approval, and never for authorization, ownership, workspace-scope,
secret-handling, data-loss, or review-gate blockers.

## Phase 0 Decision Note

Phase 0 decision-note entries are recorded in the PR00 pass history below. This
heading is the stable machine-checkable anchor for specs that cite the execution
log as the decision-note source of truth.

## Phase 0 Landing Status (2026-07-05)

PRs #46-#54 merged to `main` (merge commits `bce90e08` through `1fb5cc80`).
Per-lane `Status:` fields below were written while the stacked PRs were open
drafts and are historical; this section is the post-landing record.

What landed: the Phase 0 engine proof in `packages/workspace-engine` plus the
`crates/workspace-kernel-spike` benchmark, P0A share-revocation hardening, and
P0C desktop activity/watcher improvements. The engine is package-level proof
only: no `apps/` or `services/` code imports it yet, and no
`Phase0SharedSubstrateBaseline` package was created — the lanes shipped their
provisional symbols directly in `@dohc/workspace-engine`.

Validation at landing: local package suites passed (workspace-engine 177 tests,
workspace-history 47, workspace-fs 40, workspace-core 108, MCP 58, plus Rust
fmt/test and the local-agent smokes). The live Postgres/Docker-backed suites
could not run locally (Docker unavailable in this WSL distro); GitHub Actions
remained disabled by user direction; the P0G Codex agent smoke passed only
under `DOHC_CODEX_SANDBOX=danger-full-access`, and the Claude compatibility
smoke only with `DOHC_CLAUDE_MODEL=sonnet`, both recorded as one-off QA
exceptions.

Post-landing validation closure (2026-07-05): with Docker Desktop running and
the dev Postgres container up (`docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d
postgres`), the previously blocked live suites passed on the landing tree
plus docs-only edits: `@dohc/workspace-postgres` 23/23 tests across 8 files
including the live `conformance.test.ts`, and `@dohc/workspace-api` 76/76
tests across 10 files including the live-pg `shares.test.ts` and the
better-auth device-authorization flow. The Phase 0 external-infra validation
blocker is closed; local Docker Postgres is the enforced validation leg going
forward per User Decision 5.

Carried-forward unchecked proof-arc gates (see the Phase 0 Proof Arc gate
checklist below): shared substrate baseline package; server/engine-derived
actor identity on write paths; full workspace scoping; lock/protected-path
enforcement for agent writes; external-edit detection and startup
reconciliation through the product watcher; linked chat appearing beside the
file; agent chat display name; workspace-switch race E2E; performance
measurements and budget passes; CodeRabbit major gates. These become PR 0M
acceptance inputs.

The "expansion roadmap revised with Phase 0 findings" artifact required by the
P0G gate is now recorded in the plan:
[Phase 0 Outcome And Roadmap Revision (2026-07-05)](./2026-06-23-think-bigger-dohc-workspace-engine.md#phase-0-outcome-and-roadmap-revision-2026-07-05).
The next phase is PR 0M (Product Mount Arc) with a re-scoped PR 01; see the
plan's PR Roadmap.

Post-landing user decisions (2026-07-05), recorded in full in the plan's
User Decisions subsection of the outcome section: mount-first approved; named
versions are the PR 0M wedge surface; storage baseline is SQLite (WAL) with
SHA-256 content-addressed snapshot blobs; multiplatform write path required in
PR 0M (no Linux-only fail-closed writer); local Docker Postgres is the
enforced validation leg; CodeRabbit used sparingly at major gates via CLI or
GitHub PR review with batched fixes; the legacy stack is replaced outright
with no migration or backwards compatibility (PR 21 superseded into a legacy
retirement/salvage audit); no chat feel-test gate before the chats roadmap.

### Automated Review

- Status: deferred until the P0B major readiness/material-risk gate under the
  2026-06-29 user-directed review policy; no per-fix rerun is required for the
  P0R stack-refresh merge.
- Findings fixed in this P0B loop:
  - Major: cached state could be mutated before durable persistence completed.
  - Major: path aliases were workspace-global instead of version-scoped.
  - Major: malformed JSON escaped as a raw `SyntaxError`.
  - Critical: same-root store instances could overwrite each other because
    writes were only serialized per instance.
  - Major: `getObject()` exposed a shared `lastKnownPath` that became
    misleading when branches diverged.
  - Major: nested corrupt state could escape the store error contract.
  - Major: P0B open-PR gate wording implied a stacked-target bypass.
  - Minor: failed-persistence regression used a loose rejection assertion.
  - Critical: stale-lock recovery could delete a live replacement lock.
  - Major: heartbeat writes could finish after lock release.
  - Major: public clone helpers could leak unknown persisted properties.
  - Major: version `kind` and `forkPoint` consistency was not enforced.
  - Major: lock owner initialization failure could leave an empty lock dir.
  - Major: warm cache reads hashed the full state file.
  - Major: lock health checks could leak raw fs errors when owner metadata
    disappeared.
  - Major: atomic replacements lacked temp-file and parent-directory fsyncs.
  - Major: rename invalid-path coverage was missing.
  - Minor: lock serialization waits used exact counter equality.
- Fixes applied:
  - Added copy-on-write mutation flow and only assign `cachedState` after
    `writeFileAtomic` succeeds.
  - Moved path aliases under `VersionId` and copied aliases when forking named
    versions.
  - Wrapped JSON parse syntax failures as `VersionedTextStoreError` with
    `state-corrupt`.
  - Added a global per-store-path write chain and reload writable state from
    disk before each serialized mutation.
  - Removed shared `lastKnownPath`; version paths live on snapshots.
  - Added nested state validation and precise failed-persist regression
    coverage.
  - Tightened the P0B PR gate wording to remain blocked on PR00 and upstream
    lane decisions.
- Remaining verification:
  - Run the required CodeRabbit major gate when P0B reaches readiness or a
    material risk decision point.

    shape.
  - Warned to keep Node/fs APIs split from browser-safe surfaces and avoid
    canonical `atoms.body` assumptions.
- Architecture: pending.
- Security: pending.
- QA: pending.

### Security / Privacy Notes

- The store refuses reserved `.dohc`, traversal, absolute, and invalid paths
  through the existing core path guard.
- The store scopes every version, object, snapshot, and moment by workspace ID.
- Writes carry actor-neutral metadata only; this intentionally avoids guessing
  whether a local file write came from a human or an agent.
- Corrupt persisted state fails closed.
- No rich-doc/Y.Doc or `atoms.body` behavior is introduced.

### Performance Notes

- Budget areas touched: package-level local metadata store only.
- Metrics: focused Vitest suite completed in 3.08s locally after the P0R stack
  refresh.
- Workspace/file/chat sizes: unit fixtures cover one-file version isolation.
- Machine/CI context: local Codex machine; latest rerun used Node v24.18.0 and
  pnpm 10.24.0.
- Budget pass/fail: no UI/startup/watch budget applies yet.
- Jank/blocking notes: no renderer integration or long-running scan is added.

### Migration Notes

- Adds a new package and lockfile entry.
- Store path is `.dohc/engine/versioned-text-store.json`, but no production
  app path reads or writes it yet.
- Existing history, sync, atoms, Y.Doc, and desktop behavior are untouched.

### Remaining Risk

- This is an intentionally narrow durable JSON proof, not the final
  concurrent/multi-process storage engine.
- No production write path is integrated yet; P0C owns file/API write capture
  and history.
- No merge/conflict behavior is included; P0D owns compare, clean merge, and
  conflict preservation.
- PR00 docs-only local-agent-CLI exception and upstream lane PR approvals remain
  gates before P0B can be marked complete.
- Required CodeRabbit major-gate review and stacked PR review are still pending.

### Follow-Up / Deletion Conditions

- Promote this package into the Phase 0 file/API loop in P0C, or delete it if
  P0C chooses a different minimal engine substrate.

### Automated Review

- Status: deferred until the P0C major readiness/material-risk gate under the
  2026-06-29 user-directed review policy; no per-fix rerun is required for the
  P0B stack-refresh merge.
- Findings: the latest completed historical review against commit `a935e96`
  raised 17 issues. Sixteen produced local fixes here; one duplicated desktop
  fallback-instance concern was verified already satisfied by the root-keyed
  ephemeral store, with the related unguarded fallback read path fixed. Earlier
  completed/timed-out review findings listed below are historical and fixed in
  this lane.
- Next review gate: run CodeRabbit only when P0C reaches major readiness, gains
  a material-risk change, or enters the final P0G proof-arc hardening gate.
- Latest fixes after completed review pass against commit `a935e96`:
  - Hocuspocus admin disconnect now propagates caller abort reasons separately
    from internal timeout aborts.
  - Share revocation completion keeps `disconnect_completed` rows for the
    retention cleanup window instead of deleting them inline.
  - History lock owners now store a Linux process-start identity when available,
    so a reused live PID does not keep a stale lock unreclaimable.
  - Desktop history reads soften fallback read failures too; the repeated
    fallback-instance finding was verified already satisfied by the shared
    root-keyed ephemeral store.
  - Desktop release preflight now runs `@dohc/workspace-engine typecheck`.
  - MCP optimistic `expectedSha256` checks now run inside the atomic publish
    precondition immediately before rename/link.
  - Rust and TypeScript scan/bench paths now share the `.dohc-write-*` ignore
    contract, and the bench fixture writes exact `bytesPerFile` totals.
  - Versioned persisted-state loading allows legacy ignored-segment paths while
    new mutations still reject them.
  - Share revocation UTC regex no longer accepts year `0000`, avoiding invalid
    PostgreSQL timestamp casts in backlog stats.
  - Versioned file listing tolerates files deleted between `readdir` and open.
  - Store-lock stale checks prefer owner-file mtime over serialized heartbeat.
  - Open-file UTF-8 checks and history snapshots are bounded; oversized live
    preimages derive restorable blob hashes from verified backups.
  - Versioned write metadata now caps persisted summary/correlation id strings.
  - Share revocation tests distinguish retention cleanup deletes from
    event-specific update/delete queries.
- Previous fixes after completed review pass against commit `8cf9bc5`:
  - Share revocation retry selection now validates UTC timestamp strings inside
    each index-aligned branch, treats malformed/missing timestamps as due, and
    keeps the regex parameterized.
  - Desktop activity history reads reuse a single ephemeral fallback store per
    root so watcher-written in-memory history remains visible to list/get calls.
  - MCP visible-directory atomic staging files use the reserved `.dohc-write-*`
    prefix, and the shared scanner/watcher ignore predicate now excludes that
    prefix everywhere.
  - MCP write/import failures after parent directory creation now report the
    retained visible mutation instead of presenting the operation as fully
    rolled back.
  - History lock owner reads cap the file-handle read to
    `HISTORY_LOCK_OWNER_MAX_BYTES + 1` and reject oversized owners before
    parsing.
- Previous pass fixes after timed-out review attempt against commit `e268a03`:
  - P0A ledger docs now consistently define the pre-mint claim key as a
    deterministic workspace/object identity fingerprint; UUIDs/sequences apply
    only to the minted durable `writeObservationId`.
  - MCP history writes retry stale timestamp races with a fresh durable max
    timestamp and stable record id.
  - History lock age handling treats impossible future heartbeats as stale while
    still tolerating small clock skew and live owner PIDs.
  - Ephemeral history fallback recording now rejects equal or stale timestamps,
    matching durable store cursor ordering.
  - Share revocation worker selection now uses index-aligned pending/claimed
    timestamp branches instead of hot-path regex/nullable OR fallback predicates.
- Previous pass fixes against commit `97529b0`:
  - Share revocation results keep `revoked: true` for the persisted soft-delete
    and expose deferred live disconnects via `disconnectDeferred: true`.
  - MCP and desktop merged history readers tolerate durable read failures and
    still serve ephemeral records.
  - Desktop activity platform mocking keeps `process.platform` configurable so
    the original descriptor can be restored.
  - Exclusive copy recovery marks a target committed only after the parent
    directory sync completes.
  - `disk-mutating` recovery now conflicts instead of restoring over a live file
    that is neither the preimage nor the expected postimage.
- Previous pass fixes against commit `f156b22`:
  - Desktop watcher and MCP history writers now derive `recordedAtMs` from the
    durable max plus a per-process high-water mark before calling the strict
    monotonic history store.
  - MCP site creation marks newly created parent directories as retained visible
    mutations if a later file publish fails.
  - Desktop activity history reads merge durable disk records with
    unsupported-platform ephemeral watcher records, matching MCP read behavior.
  - Share revocation returns an explicit deferred-disconnect result when admin
    disconnect is unavailable, already claimed, or requeued after failure.
  - Pending mutation journal size is enforced before writing and raised to match
    worst-case JSON expansion of duplicated text snapshots.
  - Versioned text store corruption coverage keeps the current snapshot valid
    while corrupting `before.text`.
  - Versioned file workspace invalid-author coverage now asserts no user file or
    pending journal is left behind.
  - History lock tests share a fake owner fixture helper for future lock-schema
    changes.
- Previous pass fixes against commit `a8ba2a3`:
  - Desktop unsupported-history readback coverage now imports and uses the
    watcher-owned `DESKTOP_HISTORY_STORE_OPTIONS`.
  - Persisted history index entries validate safe `recordedAtMs` values before
    filenames, ordering, cursors, or max timestamp reads can consume them.
  - History `record()` rechecks the durable max timestamp under the history
    lock and rejects equal or stale timestamps before writing the record file.
  - Pending file-mutation recovery falls back to inline text preimages when a
    referenced disk backup file is missing, while unsafe paths and unavailable
    preimages still fail closed.
  - Pending disk backup modes must be integer chmod values in `0o000..0o777`.
  - Pending expected change sets are verified against the journal path,
    operation, preimage, and postimage before recovery can use them.
- Previous pass fixes against commit `5d097ed`:
  - Exported `VersionedFileWorkspaceError` from the workspace-engine root entry.
  - Share revocation backlog stats test now covers claimed-event fallback from
    invalid/missing `claimedAt` to `created_at`.
  - History `recordedAtMs` validation now rejects `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`,
    keeping one safe increment of headroom for max+1 timestamp generation.
  - The symlink-owner history lock test now awaits the pending record promise in
    cleanup.

### Security / Privacy Notes

- The managed file wrapper validates paths through `validateUserWritePath`.
- Unknown local file edits use `{ kind: "local", label: "Local file edit" }`
  instead of pretending to know a human or agent identity.
- Restore refuses to clobber if the live file no longer matches the history
  entry's expected current side.
- Version-store rollback derives the preimage from the recorded mutation moment
  instead of trusting caller-supplied snapshot data.
- Disk preimage rollback restores through the guarded atomic writer rather than
  copying directly onto the target path.
- Pending file writes/deletes record a durable JSON journal before mutating disk
  and recover pending disk/version/history state before later workspace reads or
  writes.
- File workspace mutations use an on-disk workspace lock so separate processes
  cannot interleave recovery, disk, version, and history writes; lock owners are
  isolated in token-scoped directories so stale reclaim cannot clobber a fresh
  owner.
- Workspace file writes create parent directories one segment at a time with
  containment checks, and workspace reads/stat/snapshot/preimage backup paths
  use no-follow file handles before reading bytes.
- Pending journals store raw backup mode bits and preallocated version mutation
  ids before irreversible disk/version steps.
- Pending journals use pre-side-effect and post-side-effect phases so restart
  recovery can tell in-progress disk/version work from completed mutations.
- Pending journals validate stored preimage snapshots during recovery.
- Linux local file writes/deletes pin the verified parent directory and perform
  final child mutation through that directory fd; non-Linux construction fails
  closed for this anchored writer pending the Rust kernel lane.
- Pending file mutation journals are root-scoped recovery artifacts. Recovery
  processes each journal under its recorded workspace/history namespace, so
  active-workspace mismatches no longer block cleanup for the shared root.
- History writes use an on-disk lock per root so separate MCP, workspace, or
  process-local callers cannot clobber `.dohc/history/index.json`; lock owners
  are isolated in token-scoped directories and each record file is durable
  before the index can point at it.
- History record filenames are generated from the validated record body.
- History storage rejects `.dohc` or `.dohc/history` symlinks that resolve
  outside the workspace before creating, locking, reading, or writing history.
- If history storage is unreadable while deciding whether a pending mutation's
  history record committed, the file workspace preserves the pending journal
  instead of rolling back under uncertainty.
- Restart recovery now has explicit assertions that it repairs disk/version
  state without synthesizing extra history entries.
- Workspace reads on Linux now open files through a verified parent directory
  handle before post-open identity checks, reducing parent-symlink race exposure.
- Stale store-lock recovery no longer restores quarantined directories over the
  live lock path after validation failure.
- Desktop history exposes local edits as their own author filter bucket.
- History lock cleanup validates `index.json.lock` containment and rejects
  symlinked lock paths before stale recovery.
- Versioned-text lock heartbeat refresh is token-checked through the currently
  opened owner file before writing.
- Versioned-text quarantined lock/reclaimer restore is identity-fenced before
  renaming a quarantine back into the live lock path.
- Versioned-text quarantine mismatch restore now rechecks the moved quarantine
  identity so a raced live lock is restored without trusting a replaced
  quarantine path.
- Malformed pending journal JSON is reported as a typed recovery failure.
- Shared-channel specs now require authoritative revocation before cleanup and
  access-safe placeholders across bodies, titles, previews, exports, and
  metadata.
- Large truncated history snapshots carry SHA-256 metadata for stale-live
  validation without storing full text.
- Root-scoped pending journals now fail closed when the stored workspace does
  not match the active workspace.
- File workspace creation is explicitly Linux-only until the Rust kernel lane
  provides portable descriptor-relative mutation support.
- File workspace creation now also verifies that `/proc/self/fd` exists and is
  accessible before enabling anchored descriptor-relative mutation.
- File mutation locks with future heartbeats and live owner PIDs are treated as
  active, preventing clock rollback from making an active lock reclaimable.
- MCP file publish revalidates the workspace-contained path before final publish
  and unchanged directory creates do not synthesize history records.
- Preserved file preimage restore copies and syncs through one exclusive
  no-follow target descriptor instead of reopening the target after copy.
- File write publish now creates the target with exclusive no-follow open under
  a verified parent fd instead of linking a temp file into place; completed
  writes do not leave an extra hard link to the live file.
- Preserved live preimage restore copies back only when the target path is still
  absent, so a concurrently recreated file is not clobbered during rollback.
- Incomplete `disk-mutating` recovery rolls back from the verified preimage
  backup without requiring a completed postimage.
- History index reads validate `index.json` containment, not only the parent
  history directory.
- Scan no longer treats `.git`, `node_modules`, nested `.dohc`, or SQLite
  sidecars as standalone workspace files.
- No HTTP/cloud write path is changed in this PR.

### Security / Privacy Notes

- Merge and conflict APIs validate paths through the same
  `validateUserWritePath` guard as ordinary version writes.
- Workspace/version ownership checks run inside the serialized store path; a
  source version from another workspace is denied.
- Conflict records preserve both sides without inserting Git conflict markers
  into user files.
- Missing fork-base state fails closed instead of inventing merge ancestry.
- Conflict resolution refuses to apply if Main no longer matches the preserved
  current side.

- Search runs over canonical engine snapshots/projections rather than raw
  `.dohc` files.
- `.env` exclusion is enforced before caller-provided file policy, so custom
  policy cannot accidentally re-include secrets.
- Chat projection search receives a policy-controlled linked-file access state;
  denied projections return only `Linked file: unavailable`.
- Search result objects for chat hits do not include file object IDs.
- Ignored/reserved path segments are filtered before file search.

### Performance Notes

- Budget areas touched: package-level in-memory search over small Phase 0
  engine snapshots and projections.
- Metrics:
  - workspace-engine tests: 36 tests in 1.71s locally.
  - Latest 2026-06-29 P0E stack refresh with Node v24.18.0 and `TMPDIR=/tmp`:
    docs link/anchor checks in repo and from `/tmp` passed for 7 files;
    workspace-engine `workspaceSearch.test.ts`, `linkedChatStore.test.ts`,
    `versionedTextMerge.test.ts`, `versionedTextStore.test.ts`, and
    `versionedFileWorkspace.test.ts` passed 175 tests in 30.55s;
    workspace-history passed 47 tests in 11.64s; workspace-engine and
    workspace-history typechecks passed.
- Machine/CI context: local Codex machine; latest rerun happened after the P0E
  restack and used Linux Node v24.18.0/Corepack for the first rerun, then the
  local Node v24.18.0/pnpm toolchain for the 2026-06-29 P0E stack refresh.
- Budget pass/fail: no renderer/startup/watch budget applies yet.
- Jank/blocking notes: no renderer integration or full-workspace scan ships in
  this PR.

### Migration Notes

- Adds a package subpath export `@dohc/workspace-engine/workspaceSearch`.
- No production app path calls this search layer yet.

### Remaining Risk

- This is a package-level smoke, not the final desktop ripgrep/search UI path.
- Effective policy is intentionally minimal; full share/member/file policy
  resolver remains for the later architecture PRs.
- Result ranking and multi-match-per-line behavior are minimal.
- PR00 docs-only local-agent-CLI exception and upstream lane PR approvals remain
  gates before P0F can be marked complete.
- Required CodeRabbit major-gate review and stacked PR review are still pending.

### Follow-Up / Deletion Conditions

- P0G must prove the integrated search/policy flow with files, linked chats,
  and local agent QA or record what blocks integration.
- Later search architecture should either promote this API or replace it with a
  shared policy-aware indexer.

- Architecture: complete.

- Security: complete.
  - Identified that active desktop/MCP/sync/search/export paths do not yet
    uniformly exclude `.env`-style secret files. P0A now records this as an
    implementation requirement, not a current guarantee.
  - Identified broad host environment inheritance and dohc cloud-token exposure
    to agent-facing MCP configuration as follow-up security work.
  - Identified weaker server/cloud path validation than local desktop path
    validation.
- QA: complete.

- Agent CLI smoke uses disposable temp workspaces only.

  `--add-dir` alone was insufficient for Claude because it allowed access
  without making relative file edits land in the temp workspace.

  `DOHC_CODEX_SANDBOX` because this machine lacks the safe sandbox helper.
- The harness redacts throwaway secret values from transcript JSON and records
  final postcondition status so a child-process success cannot mask a failed
  file edit.
- Phase 0 proof keeps local file edits actor-neutral unless a chat post
  explicitly identifies an agent.

  claimed, the full @dohc/workspace-engine suite must run on real macOS and
  Windows runners: rename-over-open-handle and O_EXCL semantics on win32,
  ELOOP/O_NOFOLLOW mapping and APFS dir-fsync on darwin, path.win32 separator
  handling in containment checks. Tracked as an arc-gate follow-up.

### Subagent Reviews

- Architecture: lane driver reviewed the VerifiedDirectoryHandle discriminated
  union and platformMode threading through ~40 helpers.
- Security: orchestrator verified per-syscall dev+ino re-verification and
  lstat refusal; portable mode never silently claims anchored guarantees; no
  production force-mode override exists.
- QA: forced-portable tests run unconditionally on Linux; capability report
  tested per platform.
- Accessibility: N/A

### Security / Privacy Notes

- Portable mode drops directory-fd pinning (impossible off Linux via Node fs):
  the TOCTOU directory-swap window is narrowed by pre-syscall dev+ino
  re-checks, not eliminated, and is explicitly reported via capabilities().
- Windows loses open-time O_NOFOLLOW; symlink refusal relies on lstat
  immediately before the operation (symlinkDefense: "lstat-only").
- Both degradations remain stronger than git or a plain editor, which perform
  path-based writes with no identity re-checks.

### Performance Notes

- Budget areas touched: none; portable mode swaps an fd open for an lstat per
  mutation — negligible.
- Budget pass/fail: pass (no measurable change).

### Migration Notes

- None.

### Remaining Risk

- Real-platform verification outstanding (macOS/Windows runners) — arc gate.

### Follow-Up / Deletion Conditions

- Add a macOS/Windows CI matrix job running the workspace-engine suite as a
  PR 0M arc-gate follow-up; remove the forced-mode hook only if real-platform
  CI makes it redundant (unlikely — keep for Linux coverage).

## PR 0N-1 - Agent-Attributed Engine Writes And Two-Way Agent Chat

Status: implemented on branch, awaiting review/merge
Branch: codex/think-bigger-0n1-agent-attribution
Worktree: /home/ice/dev/dohc-0n1-agent-attribution
Implementation workstream, if used: direct implementation by a Claude lane
(fable-5), tests-first
PR Link: (pending)
Date started: 2026-07-06
Date completed: 2026-07-06

### Scope

- [x] Optional agent author on engine moments: contracts gain
      `AgentMomentAuthor` / `MomentAuthor` (`{ kind: "agent", agentId,
      onBehalfOf, agentRunId? }`, mirroring ChangeAuthor's agent variant plus
      the locally meaningful run id); `VersionedTextMoment` /
      `VersionedTextMomentSummary` carry `author?`; writeTextFile /
      deleteTextFile accept `author?`. Snapshot and conflict metadata stay
      actor-neutral by construction — authorship is a MOMENT fact only.
- [x] Schema: one nullable `author_json` column on `moments` (JSON of the
      author shape), added lazily on open exactly like 0M-4's
      `active_versions` (no schema-version bump: additive-nullable is safe
      both directions — old readers ignore it, old writers leave it NULL =
      actor-neutral). Race-safe ALTER with re-check; fresh DDL includes the
      column. Fail-closed read validation: corrupt/hand-edited author_json is
      state-corrupt, never a valid-looking attribution.
- [x] Capture attribution: createWorkspaceEngineCapture reads the SAME live
      agent-run slot the legacy recorder read (workspaceActivity entry ->
      WorkspaceCaptureHooks.activeAgentRun -> engineCaptureGate). Settle-read
      rule kept from legacy and documented: the slot is read once when the
      batch SETTLES (captureBatch call), not when the chain drains — a run
      that ends mid-chain still owns the batches it caused; batches settling
      after the run ends are neutral. Reconciliation, version ops, and
      restore stay actor-neutral/dohc-origin as before.
- [x] MCP on flagged workspaces: recordChange/ensureRecordable read the same
      .dohc/settings.local.json the desktop reads (symlink-refused,
      size-capped, fail-closed to OFF); flagged workspaces get NO direct
      legacy .dohc/history record from MCP (was already invisible to the
      flagged UI per 0M-5; the double-record hazard ends) — the watcher +
      run slot capture the physical write with attribution. Tool results say
      `recordedBy: "workspace-engine"` instead of a changeSetId. Unflagged
      byte-for-byte (58 pre-existing MCP tests untouched and green).
      Documented honestly: an MCP client running WITHOUT a dohc-tracked run
      (external agent CLI) yields actor-neutral engine capture, per the
      unchanged actor-neutral principle.
- [x] History UI: moment rows, correlation groups (when authorship is
      uniform across the group — mixed/neutral groups never guess), and the
      diff page show "<User Name>'s agent" via the SAME chatAuthorLabel the
      chat rail uses; main derives the display name (onBehalfOf "local" ->
      cloud email / "You", any other onBehalfOf displays as-is) — the
      renderer never derives identity.
- [x] MCP chat tools (two-way rail): dohc_list_file_chats (path -> stable
      object id -> threads), dohc_read_chat (messages + read-only
      projection), dohc_reply_to_chat (posts kind=agent with the desktop's
      display-name rule: DOHC_MCP_CLOUD_EMAIL / dohc-cloud.json email /
      "You"). Flag absent/off -> honest refusal, never an empty list.
      Workspace identity from the workspace's own .dohc/manifest.json
      (registry fallback). Paths via safeResolve (lexical + realpath
      containment). Per-call store open/close so MCP never pins WAL locks
      between calls; replies retry briefly on busy after SQLite's 5s
      busy_timeout.

### Design decisions

- Author shape: separate optional `author` field beside `metadata` (NOT a
  field inside ActorNeutralWriteMetadata) — the neutral metadata type keeps
  meaning what its name says, and snapshots/conflicts (which embed that
  metadata) can never accidentally claim authorship.
- Slot-read rule: at settle, matching legacy recordBatch semantics exactly;
  stamp is a synchronous closure read + one extra column bind — no extra IO
  on the capture path.
- MCP flag detection: direct settings-file read per mutating call (small
  JSON, symlink/size guarded); no IPC to the desktop and no cache to go
  stale across desktop opens.
- Chat write contention: WAL + busy_timeout 5000 is the primary mechanism; a
  REAL two-process test (spawned child holds BEGIN IMMEDIATE, store write
  waits it out and lands) proves it. In-process competing connections would
  deadlock (node:sqlite's busy wait blocks the JS thread) — documented in
  the test; desktop and MCP only ever hold locks from separate processes.
  replyToChat adds a 3-attempt retry for holds longer than the timeout.

### Tests / validation

- workspace-engine: 214 passed (207 + 6 momentAuthor.test.ts incl. old-DB
  in-place upgrade via DROP COLUMN simulation and corrupt-author fail-closed,
  + 1 two-process chat write contention) —
  `pnpm --filter @dohc/workspace-engine test`.
- desktop vitest: 844 passed (832 + capture attribution x4, activity hook
  wiring x1, source-label/group-author mapping x7) —
  `pnpm --filter @dohc/desktop test`.
- contracts: 10 passed; repo-wide `pnpm -r typecheck` clean.
- MCP: 70 passed (58 existing + 12 engineChats.test.ts: flag detection incl.
  symlink refusal, flagged write/delete skip legacy while unflagged keeps
  it, chat tool happy path/refusals/traversal rejection, busy-error
  classification, protocol-level tool schema registration via
  InMemoryTransport).
- E2E: 19 passed (17 existing regression incl. capture/versions/history/
  chats/switch-race + 2 new workspace-agent-attribution.spec.ts: dohc-tracked
  run via the real startAgentRun IPC -> History row and diff page show
  "You's agent", post-run edit shows "Local file edit"; MCP replyToChat
  invoked from the TEST process against the running app (genuine second
  process on the same engine.db) -> rail renders "You's agent").

### Perf

- Attribution adds no measurable capture latency: the stamp is a settle-time
  closure read plus one nullable column bind. Storage bench after the
  change: sequential_writes 1000 = 4,758-5,036 ms across two runs vs the
  0M-2 recorded baseline 4,702 ms (run-to-run noise band on WSL);
  cold_open_list_and_read 62-69 ms vs 76 ms baseline.

### Remaining risk

- The desktop's history display name for onBehalfOf "local" is resolved at
  IPC-read time from the CURRENT cloud session — signing in after an agent
  run re-labels old rows from "You's agent" to "<email>'s agent". Same
  posture as the chat rail's human "You"; revisit if identity becomes
  durable per-moment.
- MCP flagged-workspace writes rely on the DESKTOP being open to capture
  history (watcher-based). An external MCP write while the desktop is closed
  is captured by the next startup reconciliation as actor-neutral offline
  edits — honest, but attribution is lost for that window.
- renameTextFile does not accept an author yet (product rename flows are
  user gestures; agent renames via MCP move arrive as delete+write and ARE
  attributed).

### What 0N-2 builds on

- WorkspaceCaptureHooks.activeAgentRun / workspaceActivity.setAgentRun is
  the run-lifecycle seam: any "Try it in a version" driver that starts a run
  through AgentIntegration.startAgentRun gets attributed capture for free.
- Engine moments now carry agentRunId — a review card can filter/stream a
  run's moments by matching author.agentRunId on listMoments pages.
- MCP chat tools give the run a two-way channel into the file rail
  (dohc_reply_to_chat) with correct display attribution.

## PR 0N-2 - Try It In A Version: The Agent-Loop Gesture

Status: implemented on branch, awaiting review/merge
Branch: codex/think-bigger-0n2-try-in-version
Worktree: /home/ice/dev/dohc-0n2-try-in-version
Implementation workstream, if used: direct implementation by a Claude lane
(fable-5), tests-first
PR Link: (pending)
Date started: 2026-07-05
Date completed: 2026-07-06

### Scope

- [x] The gesture: "Try in a version…" in the version menu opens a one-question
      task dialog; Start composes EXISTING operations in one main-side
      orchestration (agents/tryInVersion.ts): name the fork
      "Try: <first ~40 chars>" (whitespace-collapsed, code-point-safe
      truncation with …, " 2"/" 3" suffix on collision), 0M-4
      capture.createVersion (capture-first create-and-switch, serialized on
      the engine capture chain, no disk rewrite), then a dohc-tracked run —
      via AgentSessionManager.startSession when the dialog's driver probe
      found an installed agent tool (the task becomes the session prompt), or
      a bare AgentIntegration.startAgentRun the user's own agent works inside.
      Either way the run goes through AgentIntegration, so 0N-1 attribution
      applies for free. One try per workspace at a time; a blank task and an
      unflagged workspace are refused with product-vocabulary messages.
- [x] During the run: a calm banner over the editor — "An agent is trying:
      <task> — in <version>" with a Watch action that opens the EXISTING
      agent panel. No new streaming surface; the History rail and agent panel
      already stream.
- [x] Review card on run end: every terminal run path already funnels through
      AgentIntegration.endAgentRun (AgentSessionManager turn-completed /
      fatal / stop, panel Stop, the endAgentRun IPC), so ONE new
      onRunEnded hook there is the completion seam — not per-caller wiring.
      The manager turns the end signal into a review state carrying the
      changed-file count vs Main (0M-4 compareVersions on the capture chain;
      count is null — never invented — if compare fails). The card takes
      focus on appear (announced region, keyboard-first actions, no
      color-only state): Review changes (existing compare tab), Merge into
      Main (existing VersionMergeDialog incl. conflict resolution; after a
      completed merge dohc returns to Main so the folder shows the result —
      merging into an inactive Main materializes nothing until it is active),
      Keep working in it (dismiss), Set aside (back to Main; version stays
      listed). A zero-change run says so plainly and offers the way back.
- [x] IPC: tryInWorkspaceVersion / getTryInVersionState /
      dismissTryInVersionReview (channels + zod payloads/results + preload +
      main handlers; gesture double-gated on the engine flag like every
      version operation). Try state is in-memory per workspace: runs cannot
      outlive the app (quit ends them) and the versions themselves are
      durable engine state, so a lost card can never silently discard work.
- [x] Set-aside/archive decision: DEFERRED archived-flag column. "Set aside"
      switches back to Main and the version remains in the selector — at
      alpha volumes the list stays calm without a second visibility state,
      and an archived flag would touch engine schema + selector + fail-closed
      semantics this PR doesn't need. Recorded here as the rationale; no
      version deletion anywhere (no-silent-loss).

### Design decisions

- Gesture composition, not re-implementation: the manager
  (createTryInVersionSessions) only calls listVersions/createVersion/
  compareVersions on the WorkspaceEngineCapture chain plus one startRun
  closure; switch semantics come from 0M-4 create-and-switch (capture-first
  fork, active-version flip, zero disk mutation), so the dirty-editor story
  is "your unsaved changes are saved first" (dialog copy + draft flush) —
  there is nothing a fork can clobber, unlike a real switch.
- Completion event = AgentIntegration.endAgentRun. Chosen over listening to
  AgentSessionManager lifecycle events directly because the integration end
  is the single funnel BOTH driver sessions and externally-driven bare runs
  (agent panel Stop, endAgentRun IPC, e2e) pass through. A recently-ended-run
  memory (per-workspace, capped) closes the race where a driver session
  fails and finalizes before start() has returned its run id.
- Run-failure honesty: if the run cannot start after the fork was created,
  the error says the version exists and no session is recorded — the fork is
  visible in the menu, nothing to silently clean up.
- Renderer staleness fix that fell out of the review card: VersionMenu gains
  an optional refreshKey (wired to the shell's versionEpoch) because an
  EXTERNAL surface can now switch versions; without it the selector kept the
  stale try-version name after Set aside / post-merge return (regression
  test included).
- VersionMergeDialog gains an optional onOutcome ("merged" /
  "conflicts-open" / "cancelled") so the card can return to Main only after
  a COMPLETED merge; "Finish later" keeps the card so the merge can resume
  (0M-4 merge resumption re-surfaces open conflicts).

### Tests / validation

- workspace-engine: 214 passed (baseline, untouched) —
  `pnpm --filter @dohc/workspace-engine test`.
- MCP: 70 passed (baseline, untouched) — `pnpm --filter @dohc/mcp test`.
- desktop vitest: 873 passed (844 baseline + 29: tryInVersion manager x14
  incl. name collision/truncation, one-try-at-a-time, run-start failure,
  review transition with count/zero/unavailable, duplicate + not-mine end
  signals, ended-before-recorded race, fork-from-named mergeAvailable=false,
  dismiss semantics; AgentIntegration onRunEnded x1; IPC contract x2
  (payload/state shapes, blank/oversized/malformed rejections); renderer
  component x12: dialog flush-before-start + driver hand-off + disabled/
  error states, banner copy + Watch, review card focus/count/compare/keep/
  set-aside/zero-change/no-merge/failed-run, VersionMenu refreshKey
  regression) — `pnpm --filter @dohc/desktop test`.
- Repo-wide `pnpm -r typecheck` clean; `git diff --check` clean.
- E2E: new workspace-try-in-version.spec.ts (2 tests) drives the REAL
  gesture through the product UI with 0N-1's run pattern: menu -> task ->
  Start -> banner (task + version named after it) -> Watch opens the agent
  panel -> test process edits files as the agent (attributed capture into
  the try version, Main untouched) -> endAgentRun -> review card with "2
  files changed" -> History row shows "You's agent" -> Review opens the
  compare tab -> Merge into Main (existing dialog) -> auto-return to Main
  with the merged content DISK-asserted + engine-asserted; second test: a
  zero-change run says "didn't change any files", offers no merge/compare,
  and Set aside returns to Main with the try version still listed.
  Unflagged gating asserted in workspace-versions.spec.ts (gesture rejects
  "Versions are not enabled"). Driver probing pinned hermetic via
  DOHC_AGENT_*_COMMAND=/nonexistent so the host's installed agent CLIs can
  neither be spawned by CI nor pollute the perf measure.

### Perf

- Gesture latency on the 200-file corpus (after settled startup
  reconciliation), main-process measure "try-in-version-gesture" via
  desktopMarks bracketing exactly create+switch+run-start: 171 ms total
  (workspace open/gate 0 ms, fork+activate 170 ms, bare run start 1 ms);
  Start click -> banner visible 226 ms wall clock. Budget (<1 s excluding
  agent startup) met with 5x headroom; asserted in the spec
  (expect(gestureMs).toBeLessThan(1000)). Earlier 1.5-2.3 s readings were
  the driver path spawning a REAL locally-installed agent CLI — i.e. agent
  startup, which the budget excludes and the spec now pins away.

### Remaining risk

- Try sessions are in-memory: quitting mid-run ends the run (existing
  stopAll behavior) and drops the banner/card; the try version and all
  captured moments remain durable and reachable through the version menu.
  Revisit persistence if runs ever outlive the app.
- A driver-path try measures run start including driver process spawn (only
  the bare path records try-in-version-run-start); if driver startup ever
  needs a budget it should be measured as its own phase.
- The review card's changed-file count is computed once at run end; edits
  made in the try version AFTER the run ends are reflected by Review changes
  (compare recomputes) but not in the card's count line.

### What later lanes build on

- createTryInVersionSessions is the reusable "task -> fork -> attributed run
  -> review" seam; a future proof/QA lane can drive it headlessly through
  tryInWorkspaceVersion and read getTryInVersionState.
- AgentIntegration.onRunEnded is a general run-completion hook (single
  terminal funnel) for any future run-scoped UI.
- VersionMenu.refreshKey + VersionMergeDialog.onOutcome make version state
  externally drivable without staleness — any surface can now switch/merge
  and keep the selector honest.

## PR WS-F - Effective Policy Resolver

Status: implemented on branch, awaiting review/merge
Branch: codex/think-bigger-wsf-policy
Worktree: /home/ice/dev/dohc-wsf-policy
Implementation workstream, if used: codex CLI (gpt-5.5) driven by a Claude
lane (fable-5) per the codex-implementation skill; Claude reviewed the diff
line-by-line, added smol-toml, and hand-fixed the items below
PR Link: (pending)
Date started: 2026-07-06
Date completed: 2026-07-06

### Scope

This is the plan's PR 04 adapted to the shipped engine: a path/file policy
resolver over the engine that exists today — no actor permissions, sharing,
chat/export projections, or object-family hooks yet (the contracts mapping
table row was updated to say exactly that).

- [x] Policy file parsing: `.dohc/files.toml` and `.dohc/visibility.toml`
      as source-backed, engine-validated policy inputs (`writable` +
      `policyValidated` per the projection vocabulary). Real TOML parsing
      via smol-toml (pure JS, new workspace-engine dependency); strict
      shape validation on top: exactly one top-level `rule` array of
      tables, allowed keys only (`path`+`tracked`/`searchable` for
      files.toml, `path`+`visibility`/`export` for visibility.toml),
      correct types, validated globs. Any invalid rule, unknown key, or
      syntax error rejects the WHOLE file with an errors list — never
      partially applied.
- [x] `resolveEffectivePolicy(input) -> EffectivePolicyResult` in
      packages/workspace-engine/src/effectivePolicy.ts (pure, no fs):
      answers tracked/versioned/searchable/visibility/export/captureOwned
      plus the floor classification. Precedence: classifyEngineFilePath is
      computed FIRST; an ignored (.dohc/.git/node_modules/.dohc-write-*)
      or secret (.env patterns, decoded) floor returns a locked-down
      result before policy rules are even consulted — policy files can
      narrow (untrack/unsearch/hide) but can never widen. versioned and
      captureOwned mirror post-policy tracked (no separate tiers exist in
      this slice; documented inline).
- [x] Glob subset (documented in a doc comment, rejected at validation):
      slash-separated segments, no leading slash or `..`, at most one `*`
      per segment (non-slash chars), `**` only as the final whole segment
      matching strict descendants, bare `**` allowed. `?`, classes,
      braces, negation, backslashes, mid-pattern `**` all reject with a
      reason.
- [x] Capture integration: workspaceEnginePolicyFile.ts reads both files
      with the workspaceSettingsFile defensive pattern (lstat, symlink
      refusal, regular-file check, size cap; absent = defaults, invalid =
      errors + defaults). Refresh rule: `.dohc/**` is watcher-ignored so
      policy edits never produce events — instead both files are re-read
      fresh at the top of EVERY serialized capture/version task (batch
      capture, reconcile, create/switch/compare/merge/resolve/restore/
      rename), so a policy edit takes effect on the very next pass with no
      cache invalidation. Malformed policy surfaces through the existing
      onError hook ("workspace policy validation") and that pass runs with
      floor-only defaults — other files keep capturing.
- [x] Untracked semantics: live batch capture SKIPS policy-untracked
      paths (edits stop producing moments; prior moments retained); the
      next reconcile pass RETIRES a previously captured snapshot with an
      honest "Stopped tracking by policy" delete moment (the same
      never-stale-but-authoritative rule as content that stops being
      engine-ownable text) while leaving the disk file untouched.
      planMaterialization skips untracked paths on both sides so version
      switches never write or delete them.
- [x] Search integration: defaultFileVisibility in workspaceSearch.ts now
      builds its baseline from resolveEffectivePolicy (floor-only — byte
      identical behavior for workspaces without policy files); a search
      test proves the injectable fileVisibility hook composed with
      resolveEffectivePolicy honors `searchable = false` end to end.
- [x] Package wiring: `./effectivePolicy` export map entry + index.ts
      re-exports; contracts mapping-table row for
      Phase0EffectivePolicyInput/Result updated honestly.

### Security property verification (floors unoverridable)

- Reviewed by Claude line-by-line: resolveEffectivePolicy computes the
  floor first and returns the locked-down result (tracked/searchable
  false, hidden, excluded) UNCONDITIONALLY when the floor is ignored or
  secret — rules are never consulted in that branch, so no files.toml/
  visibility.toml content can unhide secrets or grant access.
- All four capture-side ownership checks (captureOnePath,
  reconcileDiskIntoVersion, assertEngineWritablePath via materialize,
  beginFileRename) route through the resolver; the only remaining
  production consumers of the bare classifier are the resolver itself and
  the engine index re-export.
- Escalation-denied test proves the rule WOULD have applied (identical
  glob shape flips behavior on a tracked-floor path) and that the same
  rule has no effect on `.env`/`config/.env`/`.dohc/**` paths.
- Enforcement is engine-side only: parsing a policy file grants nothing;
  the resolver is consulted at use time by capture and search.

### Tests / validation

- workspace-engine: 247 passed (214 baseline + 32 effectivePolicy.test.ts
  + 1 search seam test) — `pnpm --filter @dohc/workspace-engine test`.
  Covers parser accept/reject tables (syntax, unknown top-level key,
  non-array rule, missing path, unknown rule key, wrong types, invalid
  globs, whole-file rejection on any bad rule), glob match/reject tables,
  floor > policy > default precedence, later-rule-wins per explicitly-set
  field only, escalation-denied, and a no-policy-file table asserting
  resolver tracked === classifyEngineFilePath tracked for every floor
  kind (unchanged-defaults proof).
- desktop vitest: 877 passed (873 post-0N-2 baseline + 4:
  capture honors tracked=false without deleting prior moments; reconcile
  retires a policy-untracked path with "Stopped tracking by policy" and
  disk untouched; malformed policy surfaces via onError while other files
  still capture; policy-file edit honored by the very next captureBatch
  with no restart) — `TMPDIR=/tmp pnpm --filter @dohc/desktop test`.
- Typechecks clean: workspace-engine, workspace-contracts, desktop.
- `git diff --check` clean; `node scripts/check-think-bigger-doc-links.mjs`
  passes.
- Rebased onto origin/main c2f6fcbe (post-0N-2) cleanly; all counts above
  are from the rebased branch.

- codex's sandbox had no network (EAI_AGAIN), so it shipped a hand-rolled
  TOML-subset parser; Claude added smol-toml@1.7.0 (additive-only

  bare classifier to the resolver + floor story.

### Remaining risk

- Live batch capture skips (does not retire) untracked paths, so a stale
  engine snapshot can persist between a policy edit and the next
  reconcile pass (startup or any version operation). Converges on every
  pass; acceptable at alpha, revisit if search over engine snapshots
  ships before desktop search reads policy files.
- Engine-layer search default is floor-only by design (searchWorkspaceEngine
  has no workspace-root fs access); the desktop search surface must read
  `.dohc` policy the way capture does and pass rules through the
  fileVisibility hook when it adopts engine search — the seam and its
  test exist, the wiring is a later lane.
- `visibility`/`export` results are resolved and tested but have no
  consuming surface yet (exports/sharing are later PRs); only tracked/
  searchable are enforced today.

### What later lanes build on

- resolveEffectivePolicy is the ONE path-policy seam: future export,
  sharing, and status surfaces consume EffectivePolicyResult instead of
  re-deriving path rules; actor/share/projection inputs extend
  EffectivePolicyInput without touching the floor branch.
- readWorkspaceEnginePolicy + the per-task fresh-read rule is the pattern
  for any main-process consumer that needs policy (e.g. desktop search).
- The parser's whole-file rejection + onError surfacing is the template
  for future `.dohc` policy files (the allowlist can grow without new
  partial-application hazards).

### Scope

- [x] Promote the P0R spike to `crates/workspace-kernel`: a long-lived
      sidecar speaking JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio with newline-delimited
      framing (one JSON object per line — deliberately the same convention
      as the agent bridge in apps/desktop/src/agents/JsonRpcTransport.ts;
      documented in the crate's module doc-comment). Methods:
      kernel.handshake (protocolVersion 1 + capability list), kernel.scan
      (root -> sorted relative path/size/sha256/mediaType list honoring the
      shared ignore rules: .dohc/.git/node_modules segments case-insensitive
      with trailing dot/space normalization, .dohc-write-* prefixes, symlink
      skip, sqlite -wal/-shm/-journal sidecar skip — same semantics as the
      spike and packages/workspace-fs scan), kernel.hashChanged (root +
      candidate paths -> per-path sha256/size with per-path error statuses:
      missing/ignored/symlink/unsafe — one bad path never fails the call),
      kernel.reconcile (root + {path,sha256,size,mtime} manifest ->
      changed/added/removed with fresh hashes; mtime is informational input
      only, hashes are the source of truth), kernel.cancel (in-flight
      cancellation via a per-request AtomicBool registry; cancelled work
      returns error -32002). Every response carries structured
      `timingMs.total`. Streaming progress events were skipped (not cheap
      enough to justify this lane).
- [x] Bridge auth (plan non-negotiable): the parent generates a 32-byte
      CSPRNG token and passes it via the DOHC_KERNEL_TOKEN ENVIRONMENT
      variable at spawn (never argv); the kernel exits at startup without
      it. Every request must echo the token in a top-level `token` field.
      `dispatch_raw` calls `authenticate_request` FIRST — before the cancel
      registry, before the method match — and the per-method handlers only
      accept the `AuthenticatedRequest` type, which is constructible only
      by a successful token check, so filesystem work is structurally
      unreachable without auth. Missing/empty/wrong tokens are rejected
      with -32001 and a message that never echoes the expected token.
      Client-supplied actor/workspace/version identity fields are not
      schema fields anywhere; handlers read only root/paths/manifest/
      requestId, so forged identity metadata is ignored rather than
      trusted — identity/scope come only from the bound channel plus the
      root the server passes per request after binding.
- [x] Negative tests both proving directions: missing/empty/wrong token
      rejected with the AUTH error (root deliberately nonexistent so a
      filesystem error would betray ordering); forged
      actorId/workspaceId/versionId fields produce byte-identical results
      to the clean request.
- [x] TS client `packages/workspace-kernel-client`: spawn/supervise with
      exponential backoff (initialBackoffMs * 2^(failures-1), capped at
      maxBackoffMs) and a maxRestarts cap surfacing KernelUnavailableError;
      restartFailures resets after a successful response so long-lived
      clients never exhaust their budget from ancient crashes; clean
      shutdown = reject pending, SIGTERM, SIGKILL after killGraceMs
      (mirrors JsonRpcTransport.dispose). Typed per-method calls, per-call
      timeout (local rejection + best-effort kernel.cancel), AbortSignal
      cancellation, typed error hierarchy (KernelClientError /
      KernelJsonRpcError / KernelUnavailableError / KernelTimeoutError /
      KernelProtocolError).
- [x] Shared contract fixtures in `fixtures/workspace-kernel/` (scan,
      hashChanged, reconcile) consumed by BOTH `cargo test` and the client
      vitest suite against the real binary — the wire contract cannot
      drift without both sides failing.
- [x] Desktop integration, dev-flag only: when DOHC_KERNEL_SIDECAR=1 the
      startup reconciliation scan in workspaceEngineCapture's
      reconcileDiskIntoVersion routes through the kernel client (release
      binary, debug fallback, DOHC_KERNEL_BINARY_PATH override), failing
      OPEN to the existing scanWorkspaceFiles TS path on any kernel error
      and logging via the existing onError hook. Scan-only slice: the
      per-path text-read/classify pipeline stays in TS because engine
      ownership decisions (readDiskTextState) are TS policy. Flag unset =
      byte-identical default path. Packaging explicitly out of scope.
- [x] Benchmarks: scripts/workspace-kernel-spike/bench-kernel.mjs compares
      the REAL scanWorkspaceFiles (via tsx, in-process-measured, same
      methodology as the recorded P0R baseline) and a real-scanner
      reconcile equivalent (new scripts/workspace-kernel-spike/
      ts-reconcile.ts) against the kernel's scan/reconcile (measured via
      response timingMs.total) on deterministic 1,000 and 10,000-file
      fixtures.

## PR WS-B - Arc 0P Sync Design

Status: design doc landed on branch (docs only, no product code)
Branch: codex/think-bigger-wsb-sync-design
Worktree: /home/ice/dev/dohc-wsb-sync-design
Implementation workstream, if used: none (single Claude lane, design only)
PR Link: (pending)
Date started: 2026-07-06
Date completed: 2026-07-06

### Scope

Docs-only lane: design the engine-native replication protocol so Arc 0P
(the PR 21R re-cut) is implementable in bounded lanes, honoring Refined
Implementation Default 1 (local engine authoritative, cloud never) and
the Plan Completion Map's cloud-on-engine decision. No schema, engine,
desktop, or server code changed.

### Files Changed

- docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-06-think-bigger-0p-sync-design.md (new)
- docs/superpowers/plans/2026-06-23-think-bigger-docs.manifest.json
  (added the new doc)
- this execution log (this entry)

### Commands Run

- `node scripts/check-think-bigger-doc-links.mjs` — passed (9 files).

### Decisions

- Log replication scheme: multi-origin log — every replicated op is
  identified by `(originId, originSeq)` with per-origin high-water
  marks (vector-clock-lite), rejecting the single-writer lease because
  an authoritative offline-first local engine cannot refuse writes, so
  a lease hides divergence without removing the merge machinery P0D
  already shipped.
- `moment_order` (and chat `message_order`) never replicate: they stay
  per-store local pagination order; importers reallocate them with a
  deterministic `(recordedAtMs, originId, originSeq)` interleave.
  State convergence rests on per-object head checks
  (`snapshots.latest_moment_id` vs the op's before head), not on the
  display interleave.
- Divergent heads degrade to the existing P0D conflict rows
  (base/current/incoming) on both machines — never clobber.
- Secrets replicate ciphertext-only; key exchange at alpha is a
  passphrase-wrapped workspace data key stored on the relay (Argon2id
  KEK), with manual key-file transfer as the fallback.
- Server is a dumb relay: per-user buckets, content-addressed blob
  put/get/have, per-origin contiguous log append, since-cursor fetch,
  no server-side merge; machine auth salvages the existing better-auth
  device flow; explicitly not the legacy atoms API, and
  workspace-postgres stays retired per the 0N-3 audit.
- Milestones re-cut 21R-A..E as 0P-A (sync-over-a-folder proving
  semantics with no server), 0P-B (thin relay + device auth), 0P-C
  (offline rejoin + conflict E2E, absorbs 21R-C as "derived state is
  rebuilt, never replicated"), 0P-D (encrypted secrets, depends WS-C).

### Unresolved Findings / Open Questions

For the user (also in the design doc): (1) encrypt all blobs at the
relay or only secrets at alpha; (2) is bootstrap-from-relay (fresh
machine, empty folder) in 0P-B scope; (3) relay hosting — dohc-hosted
only or docker-compose self-host from day one.

### Follow-Up / Deletion Conditions

- 0P-A opens the implementation arc; legacy `packages/workspace-sync` +
  `cloudSyncEngine.ts` retire when 0P-B replaces the desktop loop
  (audit Phase C/D).

## PR WS-C - Secret-Backed Files (PR 08 On The Shipped Engine)

Status: implemented on branch, awaiting review/merge
Branch: codex/think-bigger-wsc-secrets
Worktree: /home/ice/dev/dohc-wsc-secrets
Implementation workstream, if used: single Claude lane (fable-5),
tests-first with adversarial tests as first-class deliverables
(security-critical lane).
PR Link: (pending)
Date started: 2026-07-06
Date completed: 2026-07-06

### Scope

- [x] Engine secret store (`packages/workspace-engine/src/secretFileStore.ts`):
      secret-classified paths (the WS-F floor classifier decides; policy can
      never unmark) version as AES-256-GCM ciphertext in the SAME engine.db
      (additive `secret_files` / `secret_fork_bases` / `secret_moments`
      tables, lazy-upgrade pattern like `active_versions`). Random 96-bit IV
      per write, auth tag stored, AAD binds workspace+path so ciphertext rows
      cannot be spliced across files. Moments are METADATA-ONLY by
      construction: `SecretFileMoment` has no content field at all; the
      encrypted after-state rides the moment solely to power restore.
- [x] Key custody DECISION: per-workspace data key in
      `<root>/.dohc/engine/secret.key` (0600 file, 0700 dir, exclusive-create
      settles first-write races, format-versioned `dohc-secret-key-v1:`
      prefix). The cloudCredentialStore pattern was READ and judged not
      cleanly reusable: it is an Electron-safeStorage-sealed file in the
      per-install app-data dir, not a keytar service entry — reusing it would
      (a) drag Electron main-process APIs into @dohc/workspace-engine (which
      must run under vitest/MCP/headless Node), (b) bind per-workspace engine
      data to a per-install app credential, and (c) still degrade to
      plaintext-on-disk on Linux/WSL without a secret service — the same
      boundary as a 0600 key file. The versioned format allows an
      OS-keychain wrap later without migration. Documented downgrade note:
      a same-user local process can read the key file — and can equally read
      the materialized plaintext .env beside it; dohc never claims
      per-process enforcement after plaintext materialization (Refined
      Default 8). The encryption's job is keeping secrets out of dohc's
      durable/derived/replicated surfaces. Fail-closed rules: malformed key
      file is NEVER regenerated over; tamper/wrong-key surfaces as
      decrypt-failed, never garbage plaintext.
- [x] Plaintext-store floor: versionedTextStore.writeTextFile and
      renameTextFile(toPath) now REJECT secret-classified paths
      (invalid-path), so plaintext secrets are structurally unable to enter
      snapshots/moments/blobs. classifyEngineFilePath moved to a leaf module
      (`enginePathFloor.ts`, re-exported from workspaceSearch) so both stores
      enforce the same floor without import cycles.
- [x] Capture (apps/desktop workspaceEngineCapture): secret paths stop being
      skipped — live batches and reconcile passes capture them into the
      encrypted store with metadata-only moments ("Updated .env"), content-
      equality no-op coalescing, retire-on-delete, and expected-event
      consumption. Attribution stays actor-neutral (no author on protected
      moments).
- [x] Versions: createVersion forks secret tips (verbatim ciphertext copy +
      fork-base rows); switchVersion materializes target secrets to disk and
      removes previous-only ones (never clobbering non-text/unreadable disk
      state); compareVersions appends `{path, status, protected: true}`
      entries with NO texts; mergeVersionIntoMain merges secrets whole-file,
      fork-base-aware, incoming-wins, NEVER a conflict record (conflict
      records carry side texts) — the target's prior state stays one
      protected moment back, restorable. Restore rides the encrypted path
      end-to-end (prior ciphertext copies forward; forward history).
- [x] Materialization boundary: `materializeSecretFile` is the SINGLE
      plaintext accessor, used only by dohc's own disk flows (switch/merge/
      restore — the file was already plaintext on disk, same trust boundary).
      Engine-side `assertEngineWritablePath` refuses protected content on
      non-secret paths and secret paths through the text flow.
- [x] Search: engine search cannot reach secret content (floor is checked
      BEFORE caller policy; secret store is not a search surface); desktop
      ripgrep search adds always-on `--iglob !**/*.env` / `!**/.env/**`
      after user globs plus a classifyEngineFilePath backstop in
      toSearchEntries.
- [x] MCP/agent access = DENY by default (plan agent-access default):
      dohc_read_file refuses secret paths with a clear reason;
      dohc_search_files never searches them and reports the skip honestly.
- [x] UI (minimal per lane scope): history rows show a lock
      (engine-moment-lock) and protected moments' diff page shows "Contents
      are protected" (no diff body, restore still available); the version
      compare page shows "Protected file changed" without contents.
- [x] IPC: EngineMomentRecord/EngineMomentDetailRecord and
      WorkspaceVersionFileChange gain optional `protected`; listMoments
      interleaves protected moments into text-timeline pages by a half-open
      time window keyed on the text cursor (no duplication/loss across
      pages — unit-tested).

### E2E / Visual / Manual QA

- workspace-secret-env.spec.ts passes under xvfb-run (headless WSL; no
  display server, recorded per the desktop plan's xvfb note).
- Full desktop E2E suite run on the branch after the kernel-client fix
  (results recorded in Remaining Risk if any spec is unrelated-flaky).

### Live Blockers And Overrides

- BLOCKER FOUND AND FIXED (out-of-lane, 3-line): every desktop E2E spec on
  post-Wave-1 main fails at Electron startup — WS-I's
  packages/workspace-kernel-client/src/index.ts used a TS constructor
  parameter property, and the desktop main process loads workspace
  packages as raw .ts through Node's strip-only type stripping
  (ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX -> main-process crash before the
  first window). Converted to an explicit field assignment with a comment
  pinning the constraint. Without this the lane's required E2E could not
  run at all.
- TOOLING ANOMALY (security note): while writing secretFileStore.ts, the
  written file contained an extra dead-SQL block (a no-op SELECT with an
  embedded NUL byte) that was not part of the intended code. It was
  detected by `file` reporting binary content, removed, and the final
  file was re-reviewed line-by-line. Treat as a tool glitch; flagged here
  for transparency in a security-critical lane.

### Security / Privacy Notes

- The honest boundary, stated plainly: once dohc materializes .env
  plaintext into the workspace folder (version switch/merge/restore — the
  same trust boundary as the file already sitting on disk), OS-level file
  access applies. dohc does NOT claim per-process enforcement for
  arbitrary local processes after materialization, and the data key lives
  beside the data it protects (0600 key file; see custody decision).
  What the encryption DOES guarantee: no plaintext (and nothing derived
  from it except byte length) in engine.db or any dohc durable/derived
  surface — history, diffs, search, comparisons, chats, MCP tool output —
  each backed by an adversarial test, most centrally the raw
  engine.db+WAL byte scans for a known plaintext marker.
- Metadata IS visible by design: the path (".env"), operation, byte
  length, and timestamps. Anything beyond that is a boundary violation.
- Secrets never produce conflict records because conflict records carry
  side texts; merge is whole-file incoming-wins with the target's prior
  state kept one protected (encrypted) moment back — preserve-both-sides
  via history, documented in code.
- Agent access policy: DENY by default everywhere (MCP read/search;
  engine APIs return metadata only; no chats on secret files since they
  have no text-store object id). Allow/ask tiers are future PR 08+ work.

### Remaining Risk

- Legacy (unflagged) surfaces are out of this lane's scope: the legacy
  .dohc/history recorder and its MCP list/read-change tools existed
  before this lane; WS-F-era exclusions govern them. The desktop ripgrep
  exclusions added here protect flagged AND unflagged search alike.
- Renaming .env -> notes.md re-classifies by path: the file's content
  (still on disk, user-initiated) becomes ordinary tracked text going
  forward. Path-based classification is the documented model.
- The rg glob `!**/*.env` also prunes a directory literally named
  `foo.env` (over-exclusion; safe direction).
- Key loss = protected history loss (the disk .env remains). A crash
  during first key creation can leave a truncated key file which fails
  closed; recovery is manual (delete key + secret rows). Acceptable for
  alpha; revisit with the OS-keychain wrap.
- Secret timeline is read whole per history page (unpaginated at the
  store level) — fine while .env edits are rare; revisit if protected
  moments ever become high-volume.

### Follow-Up / Deletion Conditions

- Layer an OS-keychain wrap over the key file (format is versioned for
  it) when an Electron-side custody seam is worth the coupling.
- Extend agent access policy to allow/ask/explicit tiers (plan PR 08
  tests name them) and env injection for dohc-managed launches.
- Export surfaces do not exist yet; when PR 11-era export lands, its
  redact/exclude behavior must consume the same floor and add its own
  adversarial byte-scan tests.

### Scope

- [x] FTS DECISION: node:sqlite's bundled SQLite has FTS5 (spike-verified
      live and pinned by a unit test that creates a trigram FTS5 table
      through the repo's own dependency graph). Trigram tokenizer gives
      substring matching that mirrors the linear scan's semantics; queries
      under 3 chars return null from the index layer and fall back to the
      linear scan.
- [x] INDEX SCHEMA (`engineDbSchema.ts`, lazy additive like
      `active_versions` — ENGINE_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1, existing engine.dbs
      upgrade on open): `engine_search_files_fts` (workspace_id, version_id,
      object_id, path UNINDEXED; text indexed) and
      `engine_search_chat_messages_fts` (workspace_id, thread_id, message_id
      UNINDEXED; text indexed), both `tokenize='trigram'`, plus
      `engine_search_index_state` (workspace_id, version_id, indexed_at_ms)
      recording which versions have been bulk-populated.
- [x] MAINTENANCE (`searchIndex.ts`, hooks INSIDE the existing store
      transactions so index updates commit atomically with the writes they
      describe): writeTextFileInDb upserts, deleteTextFileInDb deletes,
      renameTextFile swaps old-path row for new; linkedChatStore createThread
      indexes the title (a `__thread__` header row), sendMessage indexes
      author display name + body (with an "(agent)" marker matching the
      projection format). Zero changes to workspaceEngineCapture.ts (the
      WS-C-contended file): the store-level hooks cover every caller.
- [x] COW/FORK CORRECTNESS: a freshly forked named version has no physical
      `snapshots` rows (reads resolve through `fork_base_snapshots`), so a
      mirror-only index would be empty for it. `ensureSearchIndexForVersion`
      lazily bulk-populates a version's file rows on first indexed search
      via a snapshots-UNION-fork_base_snapshots query (COW-resolved), then
      records index state so the wholesale scan never reruns; the write
      hooks keep it current incrementally afterwards. Unit test pins:
      fork B from A, search B immediately (inherited content found), then
      one write in B is reflected without touching the rest.
- [x] POLICY: `pathIsSearchIndexed` (floor classifier + live
      files.toml/visibility.toml via resolveEffectivePolicy) gates every
      index insert — secret/ignored/untracked/unsearchable paths are never
      indexed. Defense in depth on top of WS-C's plaintext write gate, which
      now REJECTS secret-classified paths at the store boundary outright.
      Read time re-checks policy per candidate, so a policy narrowed after
      indexing stops surfacing immediately (pinned by a test that flips
      files.toml searchable=false after indexing).
- [x] ENGINE API: searchWorkspaceEngine takes the indexed path when the
      store provides ensureSearchIndex/querySearchIndex (optional seam on
      the VersionedTextStore contract), re-checks visibility per candidate,
      and re-extracts line/preview/matchStart/matchEnd through the SAME
      textMatches windowing as the linear path — identical result shape.
      Linear scan remains the fallback (no index seam, short queries, or
      zero indexed hits under a caller chatVisibility policy, where
      projections may contain linked-file text the chat index does not
      carry). Parity pinned by a fixture-corpus test comparing both paths.
- [x] DESKTOP MOUNT (main.ts searchWorkspace handler): branches on
      `activity.engineCaptureFor` (the same gate as history) — flagged
      workspaces flush the capture chain (read-your-writes) and run engine
      search over a cached per-workspace store connection (the
      linkedChatStores lazy-singleton idiom, closed at quit; search-as-you-
      type never pays a per-keystroke SQLite open/quick_check), emitting ONE
      done:true SearchResultsEvent batch. Unflagged workspaces keep the
      streamed ripgrep path untouched. Contract: optional
      surface/threadId/objectId/title fields added in lockstep to
      channels.ts's dependency-free preload validator, bridgeContract's zod
      mirror, and channels.test.ts; ripgrep entries (which never set them)
      validate unchanged.
- [x] RENDERER (minimal): SearchView renders chat groups with a Chat badge
      and the thread title; clicking a chat row opens the Chats rail on
      that thread (consume-once initialThread seam into LinkedChatsPanel).
      File results keep the existing open-at-line behavior.

### Performance Notes

- Machine: AMD Ryzen 9 7950X, WSL2 Linux 6.18, node v25.2.1, /tmp tmpfs.
- Indexed search, 10,000 files + 10,000 chat messages: 234ms cold
  (includes first-search lazy index population) — budget 500ms, met with
  2.1x headroom (bench: storageBench.ts).
- Incremental index cost, 100-file capture burst (paired runs, same
  session): main 5.77-5.80ms/file; this branch 6.09-6.75ms/file —
  ~+0.7ms/file for the per-write trigram FTS upsert. Honest framing: the
  cost IS measurable (~+12%), but total burst (~650ms) keeps 4.6x headroom
  against the plan's 3s/100-write coalesce budget; batching store
  transactions remains the recorded pre-default-on follow-up from 0M-3.

### Security / Privacy Notes

- Secret floor: index inserts run pathIsSearchIndexed (floor first), and
  WS-C's store write gate independently refuses plaintext secret paths —
  two layers between `.env` content and the FTS tables. Adversarial
  evidence at both altitudes: unit (raw FTS dump after refused direct
  store writes across the `.env.*` family) and E2E (raw FTS dump of the
  live app's engine.db after a real `.env.local` capture, plus WS-C's
  whole-file byte scan re-run green over the new search route).
- Read-time policy re-check means a stale index row can never OUTLIVE a
  policy narrowing in results; the row itself is purged on the next write
  to that file (not proactively) — see Remaining Risk.
- No new IPC surface; the search channel's added fields are optional,
  bounded, and validated on both sides of the preload boundary.

### Remaining Risk / Follow-Ups

- Rows for a path whose policy LATER turns unsearchable stay in the FTS
  table (never surfaced; purged on next write or full reindex). A policy-
  edit-triggered purge pass is a small follow-up if plaintext-at-rest of
  policy-hidden (non-secret) files matters before then.
- Engine-path search ignores caseSensitive/wholeWord/regex/include/exclude
  options (fixed-string, case-insensitive, whole-workspace) — the plan's
  PR 17 ranking/options work; the UI toggles are no-ops for flagged
  workspaces this PR.
- Engine search returns one bounded batch (50 entries — the per-event
  contract cap) vs ripgrep's streamed 2000; acceptable at alpha, revisit
  with result paging.
- ensureSearchIndexForVersion's first run for a big version happens
  synchronously on the search call (main process); 10k files measured
  ~230ms — acceptable, but a background warm at capture attach is a cheap
  improvement.
- Chat index stores title/author/body, not the full projection text; a
  query matching only projection framing could differ from the linear
  path's chat results when a caller supplies a custom chatVisibility (the
  engine falls back to linear for the zero-hit case to compensate).
