### Scope

- [x] SCHEMA OWNERSHIP HANDOFF (Phase 0 / PR 01 / PR 12 matrix): this PR is
      the PR 12 FINAL WRITER for `ChatThread`/`ThreadMessage`/read-state
      symbols. It adopts the shipped linkedChatStore (the chat-core bridge
      the desktop already runs) IN PLACE and extends it — no parallel store,
      no migration job. Read-state adoption from `chat-read-state-bridge-v0`
      is trivially satisfied: no bridge read-state rows ever shipped (the
      bridge store had no cursors), so the final cursor model starts from
      zero rows and "missing row = nothing read" is the compatible reading
      of every pre-PR-12 thread.
- [x] ENGINE SCHEMA (`engineDbSchema.ts`, lazy additive like
      `active_versions`/search — ENGINE_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1):
      `chat_channels` (workspace_id, channel_id PK; name; slug with a
      per-workspace UNIQUE index; kind; timestamps),
      `chat_thread_read_state` (workspace_id, thread_id PK;
      last_read_sequence; revision; updated_at_ms), and a nullable
      `chat_threads.channel_id` column added on open (the
      moments.author_json ALTER pattern) plus an index on
      (workspace_id, channel_id, updated_at_ms, thread_id).
- [x] ENGINE STORE (`linkedChatStore.ts`): createChannel (slug derived from
      the display name; slug is a LOOKUP ALIAS only — durable rows key on
      channelId so a rename can never fork channel state; duplicate slug =
      channel-exists), ensureGeneralChannel (idempotent; first chat use
      auto-creates "general"), listChannels (with derived threadCount +
      unreadCount rollups), findChannelBySlug, startChannelThread (thread +
      first message in ONE transaction — a failed send can never strand an
      empty thread; title optional), listChannelThreads (most recent
      activity first, derived unread), markThreadRead (monotonic, clamped
      to the real message count, server-owned revision, optional CAS via
      expectedRevision -> read-state-revision-mismatch).
- [x] UNTITLED THREADS (the anti-forum rule): threads created without a
      title store '' and every read path derives the display title from the
      first message's first line (<=80 chars + ellipsis) through ONE shared
      SQL fragment, so list/lookup/projection/search titles can never drift.
- [x] XOR OWNERSHIP (P0E rule): a thread is file-linked OR channel-owned,
      never both — structurally (createThread takes linkedFile,
      startChannelThread takes channelId, no API accepts both) AND
      fail-closed (a hand-edited row carrying both reads as state-corrupt).
      File-rail threads were NOT migrated into channels.
- [x] FTS (WS-D hooks): startChannelThread indexes the message and a
      `__thread__` header row carrying the snippet display title; channel
      messages flow through the same chat FTS as file-rail messages, so
      engine search finds them with zero search-path changes.
- [x] IPC + MAIN (zod contracts, flag-gated via requireEngineCapture, the
      cached-store idiom): listChatChannels (ensures general; also returns
      the file-linked threads with their CURRENT path resolved
      objectId->path through the cached engine store, hint fallback),
      createChatChannel, listChannelThreads, startChannelThread (author
      derived in MAIN, human, localUserDisplayName — no renderer identity),
      markChatThreadRead. sendChatMessage/listChatMessages reused unchanged
      for channel threads.
- [x] READ-STATE RULE (single-user): a HUMAN-authored send advances the
      thread cursor to include the sent message inside the same store
      transaction; agent-authored sends never touch the cursor — they are
      what the unread signal exists to surface. Lives in the STORE so the
      desktop and MCP can never disagree.
- [x] UI (Chats view, new `ChatsView.tsx` in the SidePanel behind a new
      "chats" VIEW_IDS entry; ActivityBar hides the entry for unflagged
      workspaces and a persisted "chats" activeView falls back to explorer
      without marking the workbench user-touched): channel list with unread
      pills + thread counts, channel view with thread list (unread pills,
      snippet titles) and a bottom composer where ENTER STARTS THE CHAT (no
      title prompt exists on the path), thread view reusing the SHARED
      message list + composer extracted from LinkedChats into
      `chatMessages.tsx` (authorship display "<User Name>'s agent" stays
      one implementation), a read-only "Files" grouping that cross-links
      file-rail Chats (opens the file + rail thread via the existing
      consume-once initialThread seam), Escape walks back one level (never
      stealing Escape from a composer holding a draft), every async
      response liveness-token gated.
- [x] MCP: dohc_list_channels (ensures general; returns channels + their
      threads with ids/titles so replies have real targets),
      dohc_start_channel_chat (channel by id, name, or #slug; agent
      authorship; busy retry). dohc_reply_to_chat/dohc_read_chat work
      against channel threads unchanged. All deny unflagged workspaces.

### Model Decisions vs docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-23-dohc-chats-design.md

Adopted: Channel as the container owning identity/kind; ChatThread as the
durable stream inside it; slug-as-alias with channelId-keyed durable state;
DM as a private channel subtype (kind enum); monotonic read cursors with
server-owned revision + CAS shape; workspace-scoped keys everywhere;
channel/thread/message vocabulary ("Chats" in every user-facing string).

Simplifications (each deliberate, single-user alpha):
1. ThreadReadState is keyed (workspaceId, threadId) — the spec's per-actor
   cursor tuple collapses to the one local human. Schema regains an actor
   column trivially when multi-user lands (new column + PK widening is a
   lazy additive upgrade).
2. CAS is optional-expectedRevision inside one process/one DB instead of
   the spec's full server CAS-upsert protocol; the revision is still
   store-owned and monotonic so the wire shape can harden later without a
   data migration.
3. DMs ship as the kind enum only: no canonicalizeDmParticipantIds, no
   participant table, no DM UI — there is exactly one human. The dm kind is
   stored and round-trips so seeded/agent-created DMs are not lost.
4. No ChannelVisibility/membership/notification scope — Channel rows carry
   identity + kind only; visibility stays workspace-wide like every other
   flagged surface this arc.
5. No presence, typing, reactions, message edit/delete (and therefore no
   MAC-tombstones), pinned/status fields, named subconversations, or
   shared channels (PR 18 owns share grants).
6. Thread status/lastActivityAt collapse to updated_at_ms; no
   open/closed/decided lifecycle yet.
7. No live push: the view refreshes on navigation (PR 16 notifications is
   the recorded follow-up slice that will bring change signals).
8. Channel deletion/rename: not built (create + list only this slice).
9. listChatChannels returns file-linked threads inline (one IPC round trip
   for first paint) instead of a separate ThreadLink listing API; the
   canonical ThreadLink shape stays the store's linkedFile ref from PR 0M-5.

### Scope

Docs-only lane: answer the last flag-default-on gate from the 0N-3 audit
— live rich-doc collab (Hocuspocus/Y.Doc) re-homed on the engine or
explicitly decoupled — with a design note grounded in verified code. No
engine, desktop, or server code changed.

  (new)

  (added the new doc)

### Decisions

- Architecture: **decouple-and-defer** (candidate (a)) — the engine flag
  defaults on with collab left on the legacy Hocuspocus path for shared
  cloud workspaces only; the Y.Doc engine content driver (candidate (b))
  is the committed re-home shape for the team wave, replicating Y.Doc
  updates as ops over the 0P multi-origin log; full re-home now
  (candidate (c)) rejected as wrong-order for a single-user alpha.
- Verified in code that the decoupling already exists: `collabToken`
  (main.ts:1892) fails closed to `available:false` for anything but a
  shared cloud workspace with matching credentials; the solo editor
  never constructs a Y.Doc (yjs is dynamically imported only after a
  token grant, useCollabDoc.ts:181-184; MarkdownEditor loads the
  Collaboration extension only when `collab?.ydoc` exists); nothing in
  packages/workspace-engine references Yjs/Hocuspocus; collab
  materializations already flow through writeWorkspaceText into engine
  capture as ordinary moments.
- Coexistence contract: one canonical source per doc at any instant
  (file when closed, live CRDT when a session is open); engine restore
  into a live session is an external edit through reconcileExternalEdit;
  the future (a)->(b) handoff happens only at a closed-session boundary,
  seeding the driver from the settled file (never the Hocuspocus update
  log), preserving both sides on projection mismatch.
- Milestones: G2-A pins the decoupling with tests and closes the audit
  gate item (unblocks WS-H); G2-B ships the Y.Doc driver (team wave,
  depends 0P-A); G2-C replicates updates via the multi-origin log and
  retires Hocuspocus per audit Phase D salvage.

### Unresolved Findings / Open Questions

For the user (also in the design doc): (1) at flag flip, keep cloud
co-editing available on the legacy stack or ship it dark to accelerate
Phase D; (2) is markdown fidelity sufficient across the driver handoff,
or must Y.Doc-level state (suggestions, unexported marks) survive.

### Follow-Up / Deletion Conditions

  flag before it lands.

  retires only at G2-C.

### Scope

- [x] SCHEMA (lazy additive, ENGINE_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1): new
      `binary_blobs` table (sha256 PK, byte_length, content BLOB NOT NULL)
      beside the TEXT-typed `blobs`, plus nullable
      `content_kind TEXT DEFAULT 'text'` columns on `snapshots`,
      `fork_base_snapshots`, `moments` (payload_before/payload_after/before
      sides — one moment can span a text<->binary transition), and
      `conflicts` (base/current/incoming sides), added via the
      author_json ensure-column pattern (idempotent ALTER, race-safe
      re-check). `putBinaryBlob` also writes a `text=''` anchor row into
      `blobs` so legacy `*_blob_sha256 -> blobs(sha256)` foreign keys stay
      satisfiable; `putBlob` became an UPSERT so a later text write with
      the same sha replaces the anchor with real text.
- [x] CAP: `MAX_VERSIONED_BINARY_FILE_BYTES` = 5 MiB (engine boundary,
      `file-too-large`) mirrored by `MAX_ENGINE_CAPTURE_BINARY_BYTES`
      (capture classifier). Big enough for logos/screenshots/small PDFs —
      the alpha's real asset shapes — while keeping engine.db growth and
      switch materialization O(small) per write; oversized binaries keep
      the pre-lane untracked-with-retirement behavior exactly.
- [x] STORE: `writeBinaryFile`/`readBinaryFile`/`readBinaryBlob` mirror the
      text shapes with content-kind discrimination; binary moments are
      metadata-only (sha256 + byteLength, `text: ""` sentinel, never
      content in a text field); no-op dedup is sha256-only; text<->binary
      transitions on one path preserve the object_id (honest capture
      summaries "Became a binary file" / "Became a text file").
- [x] VERSIONS: switch/merge/restore materialize binary content byte-exact
      through a new `EngineDiskWriter.writeBinaryFile` seam with
      raw-byte-sha expected-event registration. DELIBERATE BEHAVIOR FLIP:
      in-cap binaries now FOLLOW version switches (the 0M-4
      "binary untouched byte-for-byte" test now asserts bytes swap per
      version and back). Binary conflicts NEVER auto-merge: both-changed
      opens a conflict whose sides are hash references; `apply-merged` is
      rejected at the store for binary sides.
- [x] IPC/UI: `WorkspaceVersionConflict` gains `contentKind` +
      per-side `{ sha256, byteLength }` metadata (raw bytes never cross
      IPC); the conflict panel renders a "Binary file" branch reusing the
      existing keep-current/keep-incoming buttons with no combine
      affordance; history rows show a kind icon + byte size; the diff
      route shows a "Binary contents" placeholder; compare shows
      "Binary file changed" metadata-only.
- [x] SEARCH: binary snapshots are never FTS-indexed —
      `upsertFileSearchIndex` deletes-then-skips for binary (covers
      text->binary transition cleanup) and `ensureSearchIndexForVersion`
      filters `content_kind='text'`; pinned by a unit test asserting an
      empty `engine_search_files_fts`.
- [x] 0P-A HANDOFF: two `TODO(0P-A)` journal-hook markers where binary
      writes create blob/moment rows (versionedTextStore.ts putBinaryBlob
      and insertMomentRow); journaling itself deliberately not implemented
      here.

### Decisions

- Parallel BLOB table over widening `blobs`: `blobs.text NOT NULL` cannot
  hold raw bytes without a schema-version bump or a nullable rewrite;
  a sibling content-addressed table with content-kind discriminators is
  purely additive and keeps the 0P sync story symmetric (binary_blobs
  replicates exactly like blobs — content addressing stays idempotent).
- Binary bytes never cross the IPC/zod boundary; the renderer only ever
  sees sha256 + byteLength. No byte-diff UI anywhere, by design.
- 5 MiB cap keeps parity with "capped, honest alpha" — oversized assets
  keep the documented untracked/retirement path rather than a partial
  promise.

  lane).
- The `blobs` anchor row (`text=''`) for binary shas is a compatibility
  shim for legacy FK shapes; once a schema-version bump ever happens,
  the FKs should be repointed and the shim dropped.

### Migration Notes

- All schema changes are lazy-additive (three new tables plus
  `moments.sync_record_only` nullable column via the author_json
  pattern); existing engine.db files upgrade silently on open, no
  ENGINE_SCHEMA_VERSION bump, older readers unaffected.

### Remaining Risk / Follow-Ups (0P-B handoff)

- Divergence records one conflict per divergent remote op; a long remote
  chain on a conflicted object accumulates conflicts. Coalescing is a
  deliberate 0P-B follow-up (comment pinned at the insert site).
- Sync-divergence conflict ids remain per-side, but the gate fix round
  added mirrored resolve-matching: a peer's conflict.resolve first
  matches by id, then falls back to the mirrored open conflict by
  (targetVersionId, swapped current/incoming heads) with the choice and
  resolution flipped; a resolve that matches nothing is journaled +
  acked but surfaced as `pendingConflictResolves` in the import result.
  Truly symmetric conflict ids remain 0P-B.
- rollbackTextFileMutation deletes a moment but keeps its journal row
  (journal stays append-only, seqs stay contiguous). If the row was
  exported before rollback, peers keep the moment and later local writes
  degrade to a divergence conflict on rejoin — never corruption, never
  silent loss. Compensating op design belongs to 0P-B. Sync record-only
  rows themselves are rollback-inert (gate fix round): they cannot be
  rolled back and never gate another moment's rollback eligibility.
- LWW channel renames (no rename API exists yet) build on the wire-id
  identity shipped in the gate fix round.
- exportSyncBundle is stateless (`sinceCursor` optional); incremental
  cursor persistence is left to the 0P-B sync loop. A partial
  (`sinceCursor`) bundle whose version.create forkSnapshots reference
  moments/blobs outside the bundle fails closed on the importer unless
  the importer already holds them.

### Gate Fix Round (2026-07-07, Claude lane driver)

Pre-push review gate: codex line-review + CodeRabbit findings, all fixed
tests-first (each critical got a failing repro before its fix), amended
into the lane commit.

- C1 (critical, data loss): sync record-only rows leaked into public
  surfaces unmarked and rollbackTextFileMutation ACCEPTED them —
  importing a peer's divergent moment then rolling it back rewrote or
  deleted the LOCAL live snapshot from a state this store never
  materialized. Fixed: rollback fails closed (invalid-input) on
  record-only moments; the is-latest / predecessor / dependent queries
  all filter `sync_record_only = 0`; listMoments/getMoment mark the rows
  with `syncRecordOnly: true` (visible but inert — mark, don't hide).
- C2 (critical, state corruption): version.create replay copied the
  IMPORTER's current snapshots, silently absorbing local edits into the
  origin's fork (repro also tripped hydration state-corrupt). Fixed:
  createNamedVersion ships the fork-point state in the payload
  (`VersionCreatePayload.forkSnapshots`, lazy additive) and importers
  materialize the fork strictly from it (rows marked via the new
  `versions.sync_materialized` lazy column; hydration validation exempts
  only cross-fork-boundary lineage inference for them). Local
  createNamedVersion fork-point selection also gained materialized-head
  semantics (`sync_record_only = 0`).
- M1: replicated version.create snapshot copies dropped `content_kind`,
  so replicated binary forks read back as empty text. The payload path
  carries contentKind; the legacy fallback SQL copies content_kind.
- M2: rename-vs-rename with an occupied destination now models
  destination occupancy explicitly: the diverged object's conflict keeps
  both side paths, the occupant gets its own path-occupancy conflict,
  and apply-incoming performs the MOVE to incoming.path — failing closed
  (target-path-exists) while the destination is occupied by another
  object instead of silently writing at the local path.
- M3: imported conflict.resolve no longer silently drops when the peer's
  mirror row has a different id (see Remaining Risk bullet above).
- M4: exportSyncBundle clears ops/, blobs/, blobs-bin/ before writing;
  importSyncBundle reads ONLY manifest-listed origins and verifies each
  ops file against its manifest entry (per-line origin id, count,
  minSeq, maxSeq) plus a safe-origin-id filename guard.
- M5: blob hydration verifies content: every bundle blob (text and
  binary) must hash to its filename, and an INSERT OR IGNORE that skips
  an existing row verifies the existing content matches (binary anchor
  rows upgrade like putBlob); tampered files and poisoned pre-existing
  rows fail closed as state-corrupt, inside one hydration transaction.
- M6: channel wire identity (see Scope bullet): same wireId = same
  channel; same slug + different wireId = distinct channel with a
  suffixed local slug; general converges via the well-known constant.
- M7 + typed payloads: `SyncApplyResult` is a status-discriminated union
  (`applied`/`skipped`, optional `pendingConflictResolves`), and
  `SyncReplicationEnvelope` is a per-opKind discriminated payload union
  (payload types moved to workspace-contracts; stores narrow instead of
  casting).
- Trivia: applyReplicationOp contract docs on both store interfaces,
  shell-escaped copy/paste command in scripts/engine-sync-folder.ts,
  load-bearing FTS assertion (no optional chaining), UTF-8-fatal
  walkTextFiles test helper.

## PR WS-H1 - Engine Default-On + Legacy Retirement Phases A-C

Status: implemented on branch (strictly ordered commit sequence)
Branch: codex/think-bigger-wsh1-flag-flip
Worktree: /home/ice/dev/dohc-wsh1-flag-flip
Implementation workstream, if used: single Claude lane (WS-H1)
PR Link: (pending)
Date started: 2026-07-07
Date completed: 2026-07-07

### Scope

The new engine becomes THE product. Four ordered commits, each green
before the next:

1. **G2-A pinning tests + gate-list closure** — the three pinning tests
   from the WS-G2 collab design (solo rich-doc editing with zero
   Hocuspocus asserted; restore-while-open reconciliation;
   collab-materialization writes become engine moments), and the 0N-3
   audit's flag-default-on gate list checked off with per-item evidence.
2. **Flag default-on** — `experimental.workspaceEngineAlpha` defaults
   TRUE for all workspaces at open; the setting stays as an explicit
   opt-OUT escape hatch ("Use the workspace engine (default on)" under
   Settings → Advanced).
3. **Retirement Phase A (docs)** — Convex-era docs deleted/replaced;
   residual comment/config references swept.
4. **Retirement Phases B/C (code)** — the legacy history recorder and
   every surface that served it deleted; engine history is the only
   source; opted-out workspaces get the honest "History is off" notice.

### Cold-Adoption Semantics (documented honestly)

A previously-unflagged workspace (no settings file, or a settings file
with no `experimental` key — the shape every pre-flip workspace has)
opens ON THE ENGINE. The single-source default flip lives in
`workspaceSettings.ts` (the zod group default + `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_SETTINGS`);
MCP mirrors the same resolution (`isWorkspaceEngineFlagged`: absent,
missing, or unreadable settings resolve ON; a planted symlinked settings
file cannot opt a workspace out; only an explicit
`workspaceEngineAlpha: false` does). The first flagged open runs the
existing 0M-3 startup reconciliation pass, which captures the
workspace's existing tree as the engine's initial state. Legacy
`.dohc/history` stays on disk as a **read-only relic** — engine history
starts from adoption and pre-flip records are NOT migrated (User
Decision 6: replacement, not migration; MCP's read tools can still list
the relic). E2E: `workspace-engine-capture.spec.ts` "cold adoption"
(existing files + legacy relic → initial moments; relic byte-identical
after adoption, no new legacy records).

### Opt-Out Semantics (the honest consequence of retirement)

After Phase C, an explicitly opted-out workspace has NO history recorder
of any kind — the legacy recorder no longer exists. The app remains
fully functional (files edit and save, watcher still settles batches for
UI refresh and cloud-sync queueing) and says so honestly:
`SyncStatusResult.historyRecordingOff` (set when captureFor resolves to
no capture), the History rail's "History is off for this workspace"
placeholder, and a persistent notice-center notice reusing the 0M-7
capture-failure pattern. E2E: `workspace-engine-history.spec.ts`
"explicit opt-out: app works, nothing records anywhere, and the app says
history is off".

### Phase C Deletions (what died) vs Phase D Remainders (what stays and why)

Deleted (~4,100 LOC net, commit f5b4a1f3):
- `workspaceWatcher.ts` legacy branch: snapshot cache, legacy change-set

### Flip-Gate Fix Round (2026-07-07)

Codex-review findings against the WS-H1 branch, fixed as one commit
("Address flip gate findings"), tests first:

1. **Cold-adoption fragility (High).** `scanWorkspaceFiles` threw out of
   the whole recursive scan on any unreadable/racy path, and startup
   reconciliation is one background task — one bad directory prevented
   ALL existing files from seeding the engine on first open. Fix: a
   reconciliation-tolerant sibling `scanWorkspaceFilesTolerant`
   (workspace-fs) that skips-and-collects per-directory/per-entry
   failures; the strict default is unchanged for every other caller
   (sync, diff, kernel spike scripts). Reconciliation uses the tolerant
   scan, reports a DEGRADED outcome through the existing
   onCaptureOutcome/notice machinery when paths were skipped (plus an
   onError naming them), and — critically — the retire pass never
   deletes engine-tracked files under a failed path: absent from a
   degraded listing is not evidence of deletion. Version operations that
   scan internally keep failing closed exactly as the strict scan made
   them. Tests: unreadable-subdirectory and unreadable-file fixtures
   (chmod 000, restored in finally, skipped gracefully under uid 0), a
   deterministic file-deleted-mid-scan simulation (stat ENOENT between
   readdir and the per-file read), rest-of-tree-seeds + degraded-outcome
   capture tests, and a no-false-retire test.
2. **MCP history honesty post-flip (Medium).** `dohc_list_changes` /
   `dohc_read_change` read only the legacy `.dohc/history` relic, so
   agents saw "0 changes" after real engine edits. Rehomed onto engine
   moments (`listMoments`/`getMoment` over the same per-call engine.db
   open/close idiom the chat tools use), merged newest-first with the
   pre-flip legacy relic; each entry names its `source`. Legacy-only
   fields (kind, boundaryCrossings, provenance) are omitted on moments,
   not faked; moments add path/operation/versionId and read_change
   returns the full before/after payload. Reads never CREATE engine.db
   (store open initializes it, so reads check existence first).
   `dohc_sync_now` was relabeled as the LEGACY cloud path pending 0P-B —
   description only, not rewired.
3. **recordedBy honesty (Medium).** `recordedChangeFields` now consults
   the workspace flag: engine workspaces report
   `recordedBy: "workspace-engine"`; explicitly opted-out workspaces
   report `historyRecording: "off"` (naming a recorder that does not run
   would be a lie). Mutating tool descriptions carry the standalone-MCP
   caveat: capture happens via the desktop watcher while the app is
   open; a standalone write is picked up by the next startup
   reconciliation. Tests pin both shapes.
4. **`./versioned-file-workspace` quarantine (Medium).** The engine
   package still exported `createVersionedFileWorkspace`, which writes
   legacy `.dohc/history` via createChangeSetStore — a reachable package
   API after retirement. Nothing outside the package imported the
   subpath (verified), so the export was DROPPED from
   packages/workspace-engine/package.json (fail-closed by
   unreachability, preferred over a test-env gate). In-package tests
   keep importing it relatively; the module header documents the
   quarantine. It retires fully in Phase D.
5. **G2-A token assertion (Low).** Tightened to
   `expect(collabToken).toEqual({ available: false })` so a token/url
   leaking beside the refusal would fail the spec.

### Scope

Round 1 — the relay service:

- [x] NEW `services/sync-relay` (@dohc/sync-relay): a dumb authenticated
  store, raw node:http + pure fetch-handler factory (workspace-api
  conventions; hand-rolled body adapter per the sqlite-worker
  precedent), ONE server-side SQLite file (node:sqlite idiom, WAL),
  workspace-scoped tables: `sync_relay_workspaces` (bucket -> exactly
  one owner), `sync_relay_log` (UNIQUE per-origin seq; `relay_seq`
  AUTOINCREMENT purely for pagination, no merge authority), and
  `sync_relay_blobs` keyed `(workspace_id, sha256)` — blobs are scoped
  PER BUCKET, deliberately not deduped across tenants, so cross-user
  leakage is structurally impossible rather than authz-check-dependent.
- [x] Endpoints: `POST /sync/workspaces` (claim; idempotent same-user;
  404 on foreign owner), `POST /sync/:ws/log` (per-origin batch append;
  gap or seq-collision-with-different-content = atomic 409, identical
  replay = idempotent skip, empty batch = high-water probe),
  `GET /sync/:ws/log?since&limit` (relay_seq pagination, cap 500;
  since=0 IS the bootstrap path — no separate endpoint),
  `PUT/GET /sync/:ws/blobs/:sha256` (server-verified hash on PUT, 10MB
  cap), `POST /sync/:ws/blobs/have` (missing-set diff). The relay never
  parses payload_json beyond JSON validity + size caps (pinned by an
  opaque-unknown-opKind round-trip test).
- [x] Auth slice: REUSE of workspace-api's Better Auth via new subpath
  exports (`@dohc/workspace-api/auth/betterAuth`, `./auth/session`) —
  same BETTER_AUTH_SECRET + Postgres means device-flow bearer tokens
  minted by workspace-api validate at the relay with no second login
  system. Fail-closed `SYNC_RELAY_TEST_AUTH` seam mirrors workspace-api's
  DOHC_TEST_AUTH (dev/test NODE_ENV only, refuses to start otherwise,
  loopback-only bind when active).
- [x] docker-compose.self-host.yml gains the sync-relay service (own
  persistent volume for the sqlite file) and the previously-MISSING
  BETTER_AUTH_SECRET wiring for workspace-api; .env.self-host.example
  documents the shared secret + SYNC_RELAY_PORT.

Round 2 — engine client + desktop loop:

- [x] `packages/workspace-engine/src/syncApply.ts`: importSyncBundle's
  apply internals extracted transport-agnostic (hash-verified blob
  hydration incl. binary anchor rows, ref validation, k-way
  `(recordedAtMs, originId, originSeq)` merge, two-store apply
  dispatch); syncFolder.ts is now a thin folder-transport wrapper.
  Zero behavior change (339 pre-existing engine tests green unmodified).
- [x] `packages/workspace-engine/src/syncRelay.ts`: the relay client.
  Push = per-origin ops above the persisted pushed cursor, blobs/have
  diff then hash-verified PUTs, per-origin append, cursor advanced to
  the relay's currentMaxOriginSeq (relay contiguity makes that exact);
  ONE 409 recovery via empty-batch probe then fail closed. Pull = page
  `GET log?since=<persisted fetch cursor>`, hydrate missing blobs via
  GET with MANDATORY client-side sha256 re-verification, apply through
  syncApply; the fetch cursor is returned as `nextCursor` +
  `commitFetchCursor()` and committed by the desktop capture only AFTER
  disk materialization succeeds (gate fix 1 below — crash or
  materialization failure before the commit re-fetches; apply is

  RelayConflictError (409) / RelayOriginDivergedError (restored or
  cloned engine.db) / RelayBlobMissingError (relay lost a blob). Tokens

- [x] CURSOR PERSISTENCE IN ENGINE.DB (the 0P-A handoff item this lane
  owns): lazy-additive `sync_relay_cursors(workspace_id,
  relay_fetch_cursor)` + `sync_relay_push_state(workspace_id,

- [x] Desktop loop `apps/desktop/src/workspaces/relaySyncEngine.ts`

- [x] Capture-chain integration: new

  materialize pass rides the SAME serialized capture chain as batch
  capture and version operations. Fast-forwarded active-version paths
  are materialized to disk through the existing `materialize()` helper,
  which registers expected engine events (sha-matched) so the watcher's
  observation of sync writes is never re-captured as a new local

### Driver Gate Findings (fixed before commit)

- R1-C1: better-auth's toNodeHandler silently drops request bodies that
  arrive WITHOUT a content-type header, breaking raw-bytes blob PUTs.
  Codex could not catch it (sandbox denies listen(); the integration
  test skipped). Replaced with the repo's hand-rolled node:http adapter
  (sqlite-worker precedent) — the relay never mounts better-auth
  routes, it only calls auth.api.getSession.
- R1-M1: the integration helper exported WS-G1 binary ANCHOR rows
  (empty-text blobs rows beside binary_blobs) as shippable text blobs;
  fixed to exclude anchors on export and recreate them on hydrate,
  mirroring syncFolder's hydrateBinaryBlob.
- R2-M1: runRelaySync (the only new code path that writes user files to
  disk) had no test — codex mocked the capture in the loop tests.
  Driver added materialization + echo-suppression + real-user-edit-
  still-captures tests against the persisted engine.db.
- R2-M2: the secret-exclusion byte walk read only the main sqlite file;
  under WAL the fresh writes live in relay.sqlite-wal, so the absence
  assertion could false-pass. Now walks db+WAL+shm with a positive
  control (workspace.init must be present).
- Trivia: relay URL placeholder said 1787 (the sqlite-worker port);
  compose/env default is 1788.

### Security / Privacy Notes

- Isolation is structural AND behavioral: blobs/log rows are keyed by
  bucket; a non-owner is indistinguishable from an absent workspace on
  every route (adversarial byte-identical-response tests are the lane's
  blocking gate and pass). Residual accepted leak: a claim attempt on a
  foreign-owned id 404s while a fresh id succeeds — inherent to claim
  semantics; ids are UUID-shaped and unguessable.
- Tokens: bearer header only, never in URLs, never logged, 404 bodies
  are a fixed string. Desktop token stays in the safeStorage-sealed
  credential store; the relay engine receives it in-process only.
- Secrets: secret ops never journal (0P-A invariant), so the transport
  ships nothing secret by construction — now adversarially re-proven at
  the HTTP boundary and at-rest on the relay (WAL-aware byte walk).
- Client trusts nothing: blob GETs re-verify sha256 client-side; server
  re-verifies on PUT; tampered content fails closed as state-corrupt.

### Performance Notes

- Machine: AMD Ryzen 9 7950X, WSL2, node v25.2.1. sync-relay suite
  ~10s (5 child-process integration specs incl. the 10-iteration fuzz
  at ~2.4s); desktop suite 905 tests ~16s wall; engine 345 in ~35s.
- Blob hydration originally ran inside the apply-side BEGIN IMMEDIATE
  transaction, holding the write lock across network GETs. Fixed in the
  gate round below (fetch-then-begin: blobs are fetched before the
  transaction opens and hydrated synchronously inside it).

### Migration Notes

- Engine: two lazy-additive cursor tables in the existing sync DDL
  block; no ENGINE_SCHEMA_VERSION bump; older readers unaffected.
- Relay: brand-new deployment surface; schema init is idempotent
  CREATE IF NOT EXISTS on boot. Self-host operators must set ONE
  BETTER_AUTH_SECRET shared by workspace-api and sync-relay (compose
  now enforces it; this also fixed workspace-api's compose, which never
  received the secret at all).
- Desktop: credential files without relayUrl keep loading (relay sync
  simply unavailable until the user reconnects with a relay URL).

### 0P-B Gate Fix Round (codex + CodeRabbit findings, one commit)

Tests-first: every behavior fix below landed with a failing repro
before the fix (the two data-safety Highs' repros are called out).

1. Cursor-before-materialization (codex HIGH, data safety): the pull
   committed the relay fetch cursor before the desktop materialized
   pulled state to disk — a failed materialization permanently skipped
   the remote op, and a later disk reconciliation could overwrite
   pulled engine state with stale disk. Now `pullWorkspaceFromRelay`
   returns `nextCursor` + `commitFetchCursor()` and never persists the
   cursor itself; the capture's `runRelaySync` commits ONLY after
   `materialize()` succeeds. Retry passes re-report owed disk work:
   `applySyncQueues` returns its idempotently-skipped ops and the pull
   re-emits write entries for skipped REMOTE-origin paths whose active
   snapshot exists (own-origin echoes stay excluded; deletes ride the
   snapshot diff only, so a merely-referenced path can never delete an
   untracked user file). Repro (failed pre-fix): pull without commit →
   cursor was already 2; retry pull reported no disk work. Capture-side
   repro: directory squatting on the target path → materialization
   throws → commit spy must not run; unblocked retry materializes then
   commits; quiescent pass still commits.
2. Oversized binary blob hydration (codex HIGH, data safety): the
   engine forbids binaries > MAX_VERSIONED_BINARY_FILE_BYTES (5 MiB)
   locally, but the relay's 10MB MAX_BLOB_BYTES (text headroom —
   split now documented in server.ts) let an authenticated peer ship a
   binary blob peers would hydrate. `hydrateBinaryBlob` (shared by
   relay pull AND bundle import) now enforces the engine limit by
   referenced kind BEFORE insertion, failing closed as a typed
   file-too-large protocol violation; the pull path also asserts at the
   transport edge before staging. Repro (failed pre-fix): 5MiB+1 blob
   in a relay log → hydrated into binary_blobs, then died on an
   incidental apply error instead of an honest rejection.
3. 409 recovery / same-origin divergence (codex MEDIUM):
   `pushWorkspaceToRelay` now never advances pushed_seq past the local
   journal's max for an origin. A relay AHEAD of local reality (append
   result or probe above local max) or a 409 with the probe at/above
   the push cursor (same seq, different content) is a restored/cloned
   engine.db → typed RelayOriginDivergedError, fail closed (origin
   reset recovery recorded as 0P-C follow-up). The one legitimate
   recovery — relay BEHIND the cursor after relay-side data loss —
   still rewinds and retries once. Repros (failed pre-fix): restored
   older DB resolved silently with pushed_seq advanced past local max;
   post-restore divergent write was silently dropped.
4. Unbounded request buffering (CodeRabbit CRITICAL): main.ts now caps
   bodies AT THE STREAM (MAX_BLOB_BYTES + 1MB headroom) — oversized
   uploads get a flushed 413 then a destroyed socket mid-stream, and
   the request stream has an error listener (aborted uploads no longer
   crash the process). Integration-proven with a 48MB streamed PUT:
   the client cannot deliver the full body, and the server stays
   healthy (health + normal blob PUT succeed after).
5. pg.Pool error listener (CodeRabbit CRITICAL): idle-client pool
   errors are logged instead of crashing the relay; an auth-backend
   failure surfaces as a generic 5xx (unit test with a throwing
   resolveActor).
6. Pagination forward-progress guard (CodeRabbit MAJOR): a relay page
   claiming hasMore without advancing nextCursor aborts the pull with
   an error. Pre-fix repro spun a vitest worker at 96% CPU for six
   minutes before being killed.
7. Blob-miss vs workspace-miss (CodeRabbit MAJOR): the relay returns a
   distinct 404 code `blob_not_found` for a missing blob in an OWNED
   workspace (absent/foreign workspaces keep the byte-identical fixed
   404, adversarially re-asserted); the client maps it to typed
   RelayBlobMissingError instead of RelayWorkspaceUnavailableError.
8. Write lock across blob fetches (CodeRabbit MAJOR): applySyncQueues
   fetches missing blobs BEFORE `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and hydrates
   synchronously inside the transaction. Repro (failed pre-fix): a
   BEGIN IMMEDIATE probe connection inside the blob fetch hook hit
   "database is locked"; now it succeeds.
9. relaySyncEngine over-mock (CodeRabbit MAJOR): the loop tests now
   mock only the transport (vi.mock of push/pull) while the capture
   stub executes the REAL callback and the commit contract; new wiring
   test asserts push-then-pull order, exact inputs, commitFetchCursor
   invocation, and conflictsOpened folding into conflictCount.
10. Error-message leak (CodeRabbit MAJOR): unclassified errors (no
    intentional 4xx statusCode) now log server-side and answer a
    generic `{error:"internal error"}` 500 — error.message passthrough
    only for typed HttpError/Conflict and duck-typed 4xx auth errors.

C — Conflict round trip (id-asymmetry honest minimum + two REAL engine
gaps found by probing and fixed):

- [x] GAP 1 (identical-content re-conflict): the resolver's apply-
  incoming WRITE landed on the peer — whose copy already matched —
  as a fresh head-divergent conflict between two identical texts, so
  machine 2 was told "a file changed on two machines" about bytes that
  are equal, forever (heads never reconverged; every later edit
  conflicted again). Fix: content-convergent fast-forward in
  applyRemoteMomentAppend — heads diverged but same bytes at the same
  path is AGREEMENT: adopt the remote moment as the new head (rollback
  preimage localized to this store's actual previous state so the
  moment-chain hydration invariant stays honest; the imported journal
  ships the wire payload byte-identical). Both-sides-deleted converges
  as a record-only row. Repro (failed pre-fix): apply-incoming round
  trip left B one open conflict with current.text === incoming.text.
- [x] GAP 2 (silent divergence on keep-current, data safety): a
  keep-current resolution journals NO write op, and the mirrored
  conflict.resolve only flipped the peer's row — machine 1 kept "from
  A", machine 2 kept "from B", zero open conflicts anywhere, forever.
  Fix: applyMirroredIncomingState — when the mirrored resolution means
  "the peer kept ITS copy", apply that content here through the same
  in-db write path a local resolution uses, guarded by the same
  stale-target check as resolveTextConflict: if the file moved on
  locally (heads no longer match the row), a destination is occupied,
  a divergent-move destination is involved, or a binary blob is
  missing, NOTHING is touched — the conflict stays open for local
  review and the op is surfaced via pendingConflictResolves. The
  adoption write journals locally, so it replicates back and machine 1
  converges heads via GAP 1's rule. conflict.resolve paths now ride
  the pull's materialization diff (candidateMaterializationPaths), so
  the adopted copy reaches the peer's DISK, not just its engine.
- [x] pendingConflictResolves surfaced in the product: accumulated as
  `unmatchedRemoteResolves` on the sync snapshot -> SyncStatusResult ->
  a calm notice ("A choice made on another machine needs a look",
  action Open History). Engine tests pin all three behaviors:
  apply-incoming round trip converges + reconverges heads; keep-current
  applies its content consequence on the peer; a moved-on file is
  never clobbered (surfaces for review, newer local edit intact).

D — Search/FTS after sync (verified, one scale bug fixed):

- [x] Verified by reading + E2E: applyRemoteMomentAppend maintains
  engine_search_files_fts on fast-forward writes/deletes, and
  linkedChatStore.applyReplicationOp maintains thread-header/message
  FTS rows on replicated chat ops — the relay path reuses the same

- [x] SCALE BUG (would have broken every real join push-back and any

### Security / Privacy Notes

- The pasted sync code is untrusted input: its relay URL is only ever
  COMPARED (trailing-slash-insensitive) against the session's relay —
  the bearer token is never sent to a URL that arrived in a code.
- Join validates everything (code shape, session, folder provenance via
  the approved-root machinery, emptiness, relay pre-flight) before any
  local state exists; refusals are stateless.
- The mirrored-resolution apply is fail-closed toward LOCAL data: any
  mismatch with live state leaves local bytes untouched and the
  conflict open (pendingConflictResolves surfaced), never a clobber.
- E2E credential seeding uses the documented plain-token fallback
  format in a hermetic DOHC_TEST_HOME; the relay child runs with the
  dev/test-only auth seam and SIGTERM-by-pid teardown (no pattern
  kills; fixtures on /tmp per the WSL rules).

### Remaining Risk / Follow-Ups (0P-D, PR 18, arc gate)

- Join entry points beyond first-run: a machine that already has
  workspaces has no join surface yet (the cloud overlay could host the
  same JoinSyncedWorkspace panel; component is reusable as-is).
- Join blocks on full hydration (9.1s @ 1,002 files). If real
  workspaces outgrow this, split bootstrap: open the shell after the
  first page and background the tail like startup reconciliation.
- Merged resolutions (apply-merged) intentionally surface on the peer
  as a reviewable conflict (the merged write lands head-divergent with
  new content; the mirror row closes). Coalescing/auto-adopting merged
  content is future work, carried from 0P-A's conflict-coalescing item.
- Divergent-MOVE resolutions are refused by the mirror apply (kept
  open for local review) because the pull's materialization diff never
  inspects the destination path — lift together with rename-aware
  materialization if divergent moves turn out to be common.
- N>2 machines applying overlapping subsets in different orders can
  transiently hold different HEADS with identical content; the
  content-convergence rule reconverges them on the next exchange, and
  same-order replicas (the relay's deterministic interleave) are
  unaffected. Property coverage for 3-machine topologies is arc-gate
  material.
- `unmatchedRemoteResolves` is session-scoped (resets on app restart);
  the underlying conflict rows persist, so nothing is lost — but the
  notice does not resurrect after relaunch.
- Origin-reset recovery for RelayOriginDivergedError remains open
  (carried from 0P-B; error-only today).
- 0P-D consumes: the join flow is where new-machine passphrase
  enrollment will mount (join succeeds; secret materialization stays
  pending until the passphrase step).

## PR 0P-D - Encrypted Secret Replication

Status: complete; driver-verified unsandboxed; committed on lane branch, not pushed
Branch: codex/think-bigger-0pd-secret-sync
Worktree: /home/ice/dev/dohc-0pd-secret-sync
Implementation workstream: Codex round 1 for architecture and tests; planned
round 2 fixed driver review findings F0-F8.

Date completed: 2026-07-07

### Scope

- [x] Secret file writes/deletes now journal as `secret.file.put` and
  `secret.file.delete` replication ops, sharing the existing
  `replication_log` / `replication_peers` sequencing contract with moments
  and chats.
- [x] Secret ciphertext is content-addressed by sha256 of the raw ciphertext
  bytes and stored in the existing `binary_blobs` plus zero-text `blobs`
  anchor row shape, so bundle export/import and relay blob hydration remain
  unchanged.
- [x] Secret sync apply dispatches through `createSecretFileStore().applyReplicationOp`
  after normal binary blob hydration. Remote secret moments use the same
  `insertMoment` helper as local writes and update tips by deterministic
  content rank: `(recorded_at_ms, after_present,
  after_ciphertext_base64 ?? "", after_iv_base64 ?? "",
  after_auth_tag_base64 ?? "")`, descending. This removes the former
  same-timestamp divergent-write swap bug; on ties writes beat deletes on
  every machine, and write/write ties choose the lexicographically larger
  ciphertext on every machine.
- [x] Secret version forks now journal `secret.version.fork` with
  `{ toVersionId, fromVersionId, rows: [{ path, ivBase64, authTagBase64,
  ciphertextSha256, byteLength, updatedAtMs, latestMomentId }] }`. The
  payload pins the origin's fork-point encrypted tips and fork bases; the
  importer delete-then-inserts `secret_files` and `secret_fork_bases`
  without minting moments.
- [x] Secret merge/restore paths now persist copied ciphertext blobs and
  journal `secret.file.put` / `secret.file.delete`, so restored or merged
  secret tips replicate like normal writes.
- [x] Remote secret payloads fail closed before insertion: IV/tag strict
  base64 round-trip with exact GCM lengths, lowercase sha256 hex,
  integer bounded byte lengths, finite fork timestamps, and non-empty fork
  provenance strings.
- [x] Added passphrase-wrapped workspace-key envelopes:
  `dohc-key-envelope-v1`, AES-256-GCM over the 32-byte workspace data key,
  AAD-bound to `format + "\0" + workspaceId`, KEK derived with async Node
  `scrypt` (`N=2^17`, `r=8`, `p=1`, maxmem 256 MiB).
- [x] Relay stores one opaque envelope per workspace at `PUT/GET
  /sync/:ws/keys`, owner-only like blobs, with a 16 KiB cap and distinct
  `key_envelope_not_found` 404.
- [x] Desktop enable-sync has a minimal passphrase step: existing protected
  rows wrap/upload the local key; a joining machine with an existing relay
  envelope prompts, unwraps locally, and installs the key before sync starts.
- [x] Desktop Cloud status now includes local-only `workspaceSecretState`
  (`none`, `protected-key-present`, `protected-key-missing`) so an
  already-synced workspace can later protect sync with a passphrase or
  unlock protected files using the existing `cloudEnableSync` IPC path.

### Security / Privacy Notes

- Scrypt params: `N=2^17`, `r=8`, `p=1` uses roughly 128 MiB and is meant
  for a once-per-machine desktop enrollment prompt, not a hot login path.
  Argon2id remains a possible future upgrade, but async Node scrypt avoids a
  new dependency and avoids blocking the Electron/main Node event loop.
- Envelope JSON shape is exactly `{ format, saltBase64, scryptN, scryptR,
  scryptP, ivBase64, authTagBase64, ciphertextBase64 }`. The relay treats
  it as opaque JSON and never sees the passphrase, derived KEK, or data key.
- All unwrap failures collapse to `SecretKeyEnvelopeError` code
  `unwrap-failed`; wrong passphrase, tampering, bad JSON, and workspace
  splicing are intentionally not distinguished.
- JS/V8/OpenSSL cannot guarantee erasure of copied key material. The engine
  and desktop zero the Buffers they directly own as best effort only.
- Deliberate boundary change: secret ciphertext and the path may now appear
  in replication payloads, bundles, relay rows, WAL, and HTTP bodies. The
  plaintext secret content and raw workspace data key (raw bytes and base64
  key-file encoding) remain forbidden and are asserted absent.
- Relay SQLite is WAL-backed and append-only for alpha. Replaced key
  envelopes may leave old ciphertext ancestors in database/WAL history until
  SQLite checkpoint/vacuum or future GC.
- Re-running enable-sync/protect on a machine that has the workspace data
  key re-uploads the envelope and overwrites the relay's previous envelope.
  This is latest-wins by design, doubles as the alpha passphrase-change path,
  and has no envelope history.

### Migration Notes

- Engine schema reuse only: no new engine tables for secret ciphertext.
  Existing `binary_blobs` / `blobs` carry ciphertext blobs.
- Relay migration is lazy additive: `sync_relay_key_envelopes` is created on
  relay open and cascades with workspace deletion.
- Manual key-file fallback is preserved: `.dohc/engine/secret.key` keeps the
  `dohc-secret-key-v1:` format and can still be copied between machines.

### Remaining Risk / Follow-Ups

- Local secret writes always take the local tip because the local engine is
  authoritative for the materialized workspace. A machine whose clock runs
  behind an already-imported remote moment can therefore hold a lower-ranked
  tip until its next write/import. The product accepts clock-skew display
  weirdness for alpha, but this one affects tips and remains a known risk.
- Cold adoption gap: secrets written before 0P-D landed have no journal
  entries, so they do not replicate until their next local change or a
  version fork carries their encrypted tips. Acceptable pre-launch; follow-up
  migration/repair can backfill if needed.
- The Codex implementation sandbox denied loopback listen, so its own runs
  skipped the relay HTTP integration tests. The driver re-ran every suite
  unsandboxed before commit (counts above): all relay integration tests
  executed against a live relay with zero skips, and the desktop suite is
  fully green.
- Driver gate fix on the round-2 diff: `compareMomentRank` used
  `localeCompare`, which is locale-dependent and can disagree with the
  SQLite BINARY collation used by the rank `ORDER BY`; replaced with raw
  code-unit comparison so the deterministic tie-break is identical on every
  machine and inside SQL.

### Gate Fix Round (2026-07-07, Claude lane driver)

Rebased onto main 5f755435 (post 0P-C: syncApply/syncRelay/syncReplication
reshaped, CloudLogin gained the sync-code block). Conflicts in six files were
all both-sides-additive (imports/exports, CloudLogin JSX blocks, this log);
no semantic collisions. Post-rebase baselines matched (engine 373, desktop
944, relay 22, MCP 76) before any fix landed.

Findings fixed tests-first (each guard was then temporarily neutered to
prove its test fails against the pre-fix behavior — all four poison tests,
the error-shape test, and the CAS test reproduce the original bugs):

- Codex M1 (secretFileStore): secret ciphertext refs ride the 5 MiB
  binary-blob transport while secrets cap at 1 MiB plaintext, and the actual
  blob length was never checked against the declared byteLength. GCM here is
  length-preserving (tag + IV travel in their own fields), so the honest
  overhead allowance is exactly zero: `secretCiphertextBlobBySha` now
  enforces `bytes.byteLength === declared` AND `<= MAX_SECRET_FILE_BYTES`
  before any moment/tip/fork-base insert. Tests: length-mismatched poison op
  and a 1 MiB + 1 blob smuggled under the 5 MiB transport cap both reject
  with invalid-input, secret rows unpoisoned.
- Codex M2 (secretFileStore): imported secret.version.fork wiped destination
  rows then trusted payload rows blindly. No-key-safe minimum implemented:
  every fork row must byte-match the importer's own sealed source tip at the
  same path for fromVersionId (ciphertext sha + IV + auth tag + length);
  extra, missing, and duplicate rows reject; verification runs BEFORE the
  destination wipe and the whole apply is one transaction (no partial wipe).
  Honest residual: under cross-origin clock skew a legitimate fork can
  disagree with the importer's converged source tips and be rejected — fails
  the pull loudly, never corrupts state. Test: poison fork with swapped
  sealed rows rejected, previously replicated destination rows intact.
- Codex M3 + CR major (sync-relay PUT /keys): was a plain upsert — any
  authenticated stale writer could silently clobber the only recovery copy
  of the wrapped workspace key. Now create-only on first write and CAS
  thereafter (If-Match: sha256 of the envelope being replaced; byte-identical
  re-PUT stays idempotent). Replaced envelopes are RETAINED in
  sync_relay_key_envelope_history (envelope, sha, replacedAtMs, successor
  sha) — a lockout from a bad replacement stays recoverable server-side. GET
  exposes the current fingerprint (ETag) + x-key-envelope-updated-at-ms so
  clients can detect replacement. Engine uploadKeyEnvelope tries create,
  then reads the fingerprint and CAS-replaces (bounded retries — legitimate
  for the enroll path, which only runs while holding the data key), failing
  loudly with RelayConflictError if the envelope keeps moving. Tests:
  stale CAS 409, one winner in an enroll race, history retained
  byte-for-byte, client create→CAS replace, client loses a perpetual race
  loudly without clobbering.
- Codex L4 (secretKeyEnvelope): raw unwrap causes (SyntaxError text, OpenSSL
  codes) rode the standard `cause` property, which structured clone carries
  across IPC. Causes are now a non-enumerable debug-internal property; the
  public shape (name/message/code/enumerable keys/JSON) is identical across
  malformed-JSON, base64, GCM, and KDF failures — locked by test.
- Codex L5 (main.integration): the ciphertext-only byte-walk now captures
  RESPONSE bodies too (clone().arrayBuffer()), pulls into a second machine
  through the same capturing transport, and asserts positive controls on
  both directions before the negative marker/key assertions.
- CR major (syncApply): `op.payload.rows ?? []` guard in
  collectBlobHashesFromOp — a rowless fork op now reaches the store's
  fail-closed payload validation (invalid-input) instead of throwing a raw
  TypeError at the transport edge. Test locks the honest rejection.
- CR major (secretKeyEnvelope.test): the "writes no local key file"
  assertion was tautological (nothing ever targeted that root). Deleted
  honestly with a scope note; the enrollment-side property is now locked
  where it lives: installWorkspaceDataKey validates BEFORE touching the
  filesystem (meaningful ENOENT assertion), re-installs the same key
  idempotently, and never overwrites a different existing key.

Recorded minors (deliberately NOT fixed this round; listed for the arc
gate): syncFolder.test restore uses `updated.moment?.id ?? ""` instead of
asserting the moment id; CloudLogin passphrase UX is driven by regex over
main-process error strings (wants a structured IPC error code);
no minimum passphrase length floor in main.ts wrap path;
secretKeyEnvelope wrapWorkspaceDataKey length-check throws before the
zeroing finally and wrap errors are not normalized like unwrap;
secretKeyEnvelope.test manual-fallback test has a dead .catch() setup
branch; CloudLogin.test lacks the unlock-failure-path regression test;
syncApply's finally closes the three stores sequentially (a throwing close
leaks the rest); workspace-contracts secret payloads carry no key id for
future rotation (intentional single-key MVP deferral, confirm at rotation
time). The "future-dated log entry" finding resolved itself (dates are
accurate as of this round); the "second-PUT overwrite regression test"
finding is superseded by the CAS suite.

Verification (all green, unsandboxed): engine 381 (373 + 8), desktop 944,
relay 23 (22 + 1, all 8 HTTP integration tests executed live including the
two-machine passphrase round-trip and the two-direction byte-walk), MCP 76,

### Scope

Shares rebuilt on the RELAY (engine-native cloud), per the Plan Completion
Map — not on the legacy workspace-api stack. The legacy share/invite/member
IPC + ShareDialog remain in the tree but are UNWIRED from the shell (they
retire with WS-H legacy retirement).

- [x] Relay share grants: `sync_relay_shares` (share id, workspace,
      granter, recipient, selector JSON, createdAt, revokedAt nullable);
      routes: `POST /sync/:ws/shares` (owner-only), `GET /sync/shares`
      (granted + received listings), `GET /sync/shares/:id` (recipient
      metadata), `POST /sync/shares/:id/revoke` (granter-only, idempotent),
      `GET /sync/shares/:id/log` (filtered since-cursor fetch),
      `GET /sync/shares/:id/blobs/:sha256` (allowlisted blob fetch).
      Recipient addressing by user id or email; email resolution against
      Better Auth's user table in production, `<user>@dohc.test` in the
      test-auth seam. Workspace id `shares` reserved (route namespace).
- [x] Server-side filter as THE security boundary
      (`services/sync-relay/src/shareFilter.ts`): strict fail-closed
      allowlist — `moment.append` (target version match + EVERY referenced
      path inside the selector + engine-tracked), `version.create` for the
      shared version with forkSnapshots REDACTED to the selector,
      `workspace.init` served with an empty payload. Everything else
      (chats, conflicts, secret ops, unknown kinds, malformed payloads) is
      excluded. Blob access requires reachability through an allowed op.
      Every recipient-route denial (absent share, revoked, not-recipient,
      unshared path/blob, granter probing recipient routes) is the
      byte-identical generic 404.
- [x] Secrets are structurally unshareable — TRIPLE gate: (1) grant-time
      selector validation refuses secret-classified paths (shared
      classifier `classifyEngineFilePath` via the new
      `@dohc/workspace-engine/enginePathFloor` subpath export, including
      percent-encoded disguises); (2) the per-op filter re-classifies every
      path and denies all `secret.*` op kinds outright; (3) the recipient
      client re-classifies before replaying (a misbehaving relay cannot
      plant secret or traversal paths into the local view). No shared keys
      route exists — the recipient can never fetch the key envelope through
      a share.
- [x] Live-follow read-only chosen (documented in shareFilter.ts): the
      recipient reuses since-cursor fetch with the server-side filter, so
      granter edits arrive on refresh; a point-in-time snapshot format was
      rejected as a parallel pipeline. Cursor advances over filtered-out
      rows so pagination cannot stall.
- [x] Recipient client (`packages/workspace-engine/src/syncShareView.ts`):
      a filtered stream has per-origin seq gaps by construction and
      `applyReplicationOp` fails closed on gaps — so a shared view is NOT a
      sync replica. Instead allowed ops REPLAY as ordinary local engine
      writes into a private store (files on the view's main, history
      moments with the ops' original actor-neutral metadata, renames as
      delete+write, version-share fork snapshots as seed writes).
      Content-compared replay makes crash-retry idempotent; commitCursor
      after materialization mirrors pullWorkspaceFromRelay's contract.
- [x] Desktop grant side: "Share…" on files/folders (explorer context
      menu, main-owned; offered only on synced non-shared-view workspaces)
      and on the file inspector's share button; "Share this version…" in
      the version menu; RelayShareDialog → recipient email → share code
      `dohc-share:<shareId>:<relayUrl>` (same canonicalization module as
      sync codes — buildShareCode/parseShareCode in syncCode.ts);
      "Shared by me" management list with end-share + copy-code under
      Settings → Cloud.
- [x] Desktop receive side: "Open a share someone sent you" on first-run
      and "Open a share…" in the workspace switcher; signed-in gate;
      relay-URL match gate (token never sent to a pasted URL — same rule
      as join); pre-flight share fetch BEFORE any local state; empty-folder
      requirement; full rollback on a failed first pull. The shared view is
      a registry entry with `shareView { shareId, granterEmail, ended }`:
      read-only banner with Refresh, writes refused at the IPC boundary
      ("This is a shared view — ask <granter> for changes."), reduced
      explorer menu, no engine capture/watcher, no push ever. Revocation:
      next refresh surfaces "This share was ended…", persists `ended`, and
      the local copy stays readable but stops refreshing.

### Security / Privacy Notes

- The server-side filter is the boundary; the recipient's fetch can never
  return ops/blobs outside the selector, and every denial is byte-identical
  to nonexistence (no probing oracle for share ids, paths, or blob hashes).
- The relay deliberately relaxes "never parses payloads" in ONE direction
  for shares: it READS well-known path/version/hash fields and REDACTS one
  field (forkSnapshots); unrecognized shapes are excluded, never passed.
- Grant-side and receive-side token handling reuses the join flow's rule:
  the bearer only ever goes to the relay the machine signed in with; pasted
  codes are untrusted input.
- Revoked shares vanish from the recipient's listings entirely (metadata
  incl. path names stops being readable post-revocation).
- Recipient email resolution reveals account existence to a granter typing
  an email (deliberate, standard for share-by-email; recorded).
- Received-share listings omit the granter's workspace id.

### Performance Notes

- Budget areas touched: relay log fetch (per-op JSON parse + filter on
  shared-log pages only; owner paths unchanged), shared blob fetch (LIKE
  scan over payload_json per blob request — O(log size), acceptable at
  alpha, index/caching deferred), recipient replay (full history blob
  fetch for shared paths).
- Baseline profile: unchanged owner-path behavior; E2E timings above.
- Budget pass/fail: pass (no regression on existing perf specs; chats perf
  spec re-run green).
- Regression risk: shared-log filtering is per-request CPU on the relay;
  bounded by page size 500.
- Follow-up required: blob-allowlist index if share fan-out grows.

### Migration Notes

- Relay DB: additive table + indexes via CREATE IF NOT EXISTS; no
  migration needed. Engine DB: no schema change (share cursor reuses
  sync_relay_cursors). Registry: additive optional `shareView` field.
- Legacy workspace-api shares (atomPath/capability model) are no longer
  reachable from the shell UI; handlers/dialog retire with WS-H Phase D.

### Remaining Risk

- Boundary-crossing renames (into/out of the selector) are excluded
  fail-closed: the recipient's copy of a renamed-away file goes stale until
  its next in-boundary write (documented in shareFilter.ts).
- A crash between replay and cursor commit can duplicate history moments in
  the recipient's PRIVATE view store on retry (state converges; bounded to
  one delta; content-compare makes clean retries no-ops).
- Recipient disk copies are plain files: a recipient can edit them with
  external tools (their machine, their bytes); dohc refuses its own write
  paths and a refresh re-materializes changed shared paths. Local edits to
  paths the granter never touches again are not clobbered — acceptable and
  honest for read-only-at-alpha.
- The relay share filter duplicates knowledge of op payload shapes; a new
  path-carrying op kind added to the engine is EXCLUDED by default (fail
  closed — safe, but shares silently won't carry it until the filter
  learns it).

- Wave 4: #74 engine default-on + legacy retirement Phases A-C, #75 sync relay
  + desktop sync loop (0P-B), #76 multi-machine sync product flow + offline
  rejoin (0P-C), #77 encrypted secret replication (0P-D), #78 external
  read-only shares (PR 18).

### What shipped

Versioned workspace (named versions, history moments, restore, 3-way merge +
conflict preservation, capped binary versioning) on a per-workspace SQLite
store with content-addressed blobs; watcher-backed normal-folder capture with
a tolerant cold-adoption scan; the agent loop (attributed engine writes,
two-way agent chat, "Try in a version"); effective policy + .dohc policy
files; secret-backed .env (AES-256-GCM, metadata-only history, materialize-
only exit); indexed policy-aware FTS5 search across files and chats; workspace
Chats (channels, threads, monotonic read cursors, the Chats view); a Rust
workspace-kernel sidecar (JSON-RPC, token-bound, ~40x scan) behind a dev flag;
engine-native multi-machine sync (multi-origin log, folder bundles + a dumb
authenticated relay, offline rejoin with P0D-shaped conflicts, join-by-code,
encrypted secret replication with passphrase-wrapped key envelopes); and
external read-only shares with a fail-closed server-side selector filter.

### Explicitly deferred (recorded, not forgotten)

- Legacy cloud stack retirement Phase D (workspace-api / hocuspocus /
  workspace-postgres / apps/web as a coupled unit) — the engine-native relay
  supersedes it; retirement is mechanical follow-up.
- Rich-doc live collaboration re-home on the engine (WS-G2 candidate (b):
  Y.Doc content driver + update-ops over the sync log) — decoupled and
  deferred to the team wave; solo rich-doc editing works today with zero
  Hocuspocus.
- Chats: notifications/mentions (PR 16), DMs UI, presence/typing/reactions,
  shared channels; PR 18 covers file/version shares, not chat shares.
- Sync: conflict-id symmetry, conflict coalescing, rollback compensating ops,
  origin-reset recovery, relay GC/quotas (0P follow-ups).
- Rust kernel packaging for macOS/Windows; the sidecar stays dev-flagged.

### Remaining alpha caveats

- macOS/Windows real-runner validation is outstanding (the portable writer and
  the whole suite are logic-verified on Linux). This is the gate before any
  real Windows release build — the user's daily platform.
- Passphrase-wrapped secret sync uses scrypt (Argon2id is a dependency-cost
  upgrade); pre-0P-D secrets replicate on next change.
- Per-lane CodeRabbit minor/trivial findings were recorded across the lane
  entries above for a consolidated arc-gate cleanup sweep.

### Validation at completion (main 060fa06b, 2026-07-07)

Local package suites green after a clean install: workspace-engine 389,
desktop 960, sync-relay 53 (live child-process relay), workspace-contracts 10,
workspace-core 108, workspace-history 47, workspace-fs 44, mcp 80,
workspace-api 76 (live Postgres), workspace-postgres 23 (live Postgres);
repo-wide typecheck clean; docs link checker green. GitHub Actions remain

### The one thing no gate can do

Dogfooding. The engine is the default and every loop is tested and reviewed,
but the product's promise is a *feel* — flip a real workspace, work in a named
version for a day, hand a task to an agent with "Try in a version", and let
the friction reshape the next phase more than any document does.

## Y.Doc Engine Driver Design (G2-B/C)

Design-only lane (no product code). Added
`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-07-think-bigger-ydoc-engine-driver-design.md`
(manifest + doc-links checker green), designing WS-G2 candidate (b): the
Y.Doc as an engine content driver, so live collab can retire off Hocuspocus.

- **Storage.** A rich doc stays a `file_objects` row; three lazy-additive
  tables (`ydoc_docs` head pointers, `ydoc_updates` append-only log,
  `ydoc_snapshots`) file Y.Doc state under `(workspace_id, version_id,
  object_id)`. Update/snapshot bytes are content-addressed into the existing
  `binary_blobs` (engineDbSchema.ts), which POSITIONS Y.Doc state to ride the
  0P blob path — but at G2-B those blobs are LOCAL-ONLY: no replication op
  references them, so they do NOT replicate yet (that arrives with the
  `ydoc.update` op in G2-C). Until then a Y.Doc's cross-device story is its
  settled `.md` (markdown-is-the-artifact). The local blob GC must treat a blob
  referenced by a live `ydoc_updates`/`ydoc_snapshots` head as a ROOT (never an
  orphan). The markdown `snapshots.text` + `moments` stay
  as the PROJECTION beside the Y.Doc — searchable/exportable/restorable and
  the durable artifact. `content_kind` stays `text`; the driver dimension is
  the `ydoc_docs` marker.
- **Projection + handoff.** Settle on quiesce writes markdown via
  `writeTextFile` (a normal capture moment) using the salvaged
  `yDocToMarkdown`; open seeds via `markdownToYDoc`. Canonical flips
  file->Y.Doc on session open and Y.Doc->file on session close, never both
  (WS-G2 rule extended). Version switch = closed-session boundary; restore
  into a live doc = external edit reconciled by the shipped
  `reconcileExternalEdit`; cross-version merge = projection three-way with
  P0D preserve-both (the CRDT has no cross-version ancestry).
- **`ydoc.update` replication (G2-C).** New op kind in the multi-origin log,
  standard `(originId, originSeq)` envelope, update bytes shipped as a
  content-addressed blob over the existing relay push/fetch. Commutative CRDT
  deltas: apply is `Y.applyUpdate` + re-project, with NO head check and NO
  P0D conflict machinery (convergence is Yjs, not the log). Awareness is
  ephemeral, never journaled, over a separate relay channel. Low-latency is
  the same ops pushed instead of polled.
- **Retirement.** Delete `services/hocuspocus`, the `POST /workspaces/:id/
  collab/token` route, and the renderer Hocuspocus provider; keep
  `collabSession.ts` (reused by the engine provider). Salvage
  `import-export.ts`/`dohc-markdown-extensions.ts`. Cutover at a closed-
  session boundary (WS-G2 rule 5); no update-history migration.
- **Milestones.** G2-B: storage+compaction -> projection+capture ->
  editor-binding-for-solo -> driver behavior matrix. G2-C: `ydoc.update`
  replication -> awareness+relay-push -> Hocuspocus retirement. Each with a
  test gate. Three user questions: markdown-fidelity-vs-full-Y.Doc-state;
  solo-on-Y.Doc-now vs plain-autosave-until-G2-C; re-home vs retire the
  suggestions/semantic-api surfaces.

The deferred full retirement: `packages/workspace-history` and

code was moved verbatim, proven by its tests moving with it.

  pure, browser-safe 3-way text merge moved verbatim to

  `@dohc/workspace-core/mergeMarkdown` subpath (mirroring the old dedicated
  subpath; deliberately NOT on the core barrel, which pulls node:fs via

  → engine-internal.** `changeSetStore.ts` (+ its test) moved verbatim to
  `packages/workspace-engine/src/changeSetStore.ts`; it imports only node: and

  caller, via the quarantined `versionedFileWorkspace.ts`) is edge-free.

  no cross-package import. The engine index re-exports `createChangeSetStore` +

  production surface records through it) for the two remaining external readers:

## Turn On The Rust Kernel

Status: implemented on branch, awaiting review/merge
Branch: codex/kernel-turn-on
Worktree: /home/ice/dev/dohc-r3-kernel-on
Implementation workstream: codex CLI (gpt-5.5) drove the bulk implementation
in one `codex exec` round per the codex-implementation skill; a Claude lane
(fable-5) scoped the self-contained prompt, reviewed the fail-open resolution
wrapper and the build gating line-by-line (the whole safety argument is "every
error falls back to TS"), added the `.gitignore` for the staged host binary,
and ran every verification command itself (codex's sandbox blocked the bench
and the full desktop suite; both are green unsandboxed).
Date started: 2026-07-07
Date completed: 2026-07-07

### Scope

- [x] PACKAGING/BUILD: new `apps/desktop/scripts/build-workspace-kernel.mjs`
      runs `cargo build --release --manifest-path
      <repoRoot>/crates/workspace-kernel/Cargo.toml` and stages the host
      binary to `apps/desktop/resources/workspace-kernel/
      dohc-workspace-kernel[.exe]`. GATED TO DEGRADE, NEVER FAIL: exits 0 with
      a warning on `DOHC_SKIP_WORKSPACE_KERNEL_BUILD=1`, missing cargo
      (spawn ENOENT), a nonzero cargo build, or a missing build artifact — so
      a machine/CI job with no Rust toolchain still produces a working JS
      build that ships without a bundled binary and runs the TS path at
      runtime. Wired into the desktop `build` and `package` npm scripts before
      `electron-vite build` (mirrors the existing
      `ensure-electron-installed.mjs` chaining). electron-builder ships the
      staged directory as an unpacked `extraResources` entry (`from:
      resources/workspace-kernel` -> `to: workspace-kernel`), outside
      `app.asar` (a native binary must never live inside asar). The staged dir
      is `.gitignore`d (platform-specific, rebuilt per machine/CI job).
- [x] RUNTIME RESOLUTION: `@dohc/workspace-kernel-client` gains
      `defaultWorkspaceKernelPackagedBinaryPath({isPackaged, resourcesPath,
      platform})` and stays framework-agnostic (zero Electron import — the
      desktop side injects `app.isPackaged` + `process.resourcesPath` via
      `configureWorkspaceKernelRuntime`). Dev-path defaults switched from
      `process.cwd()` to `repoRootFromPackage()`. Resolution order: packaged
      resource path, `DOHC_KERNEL_BINARY_PATH` override, repo release, repo
      debug — first existing wins.
- [x] TURN ON (safely): replaced the opt-in `DOHC_KERNEL_SIDECAR !== "1"` gate
      in `scanWorkspaceFilesForReconcile` with default-on selection. The
      kernel is used when a candidate binary EXISTS on disk; any error class
      (spawn failure, ENOENT, wrong platform/arch, timeout, crash, protocol
      error, or a kernel-side scan error) is caught and falls open to
      `scanWorkspaceFilesTolerant`. `DOHC_KERNEL_SIDECAR=0` is an explicit
      force-off escape hatch (straight to TS, no resolution, no spawn). No
      candidate binary = silent TS path with NO fallback-log noise (so every
      Windows machine without a bundled binary stays quiet until the CI
      matrix ships one).
- [x] ROBUSTNESS: process-lifetime disable-after-N guard. Module-level
      `WORKSPACE_KERNEL_FAILURE_DISABLE_THRESHOLD = 3`: three consecutive
      attempted-kernel failures trip `workspaceKernelDisabledForProcess`, after
      which every workspace's reconcile scan in that process goes straight to
      TS until restart (no thrashing a broken binary each reconcile). A
      successful kernel scan resets the counter to 0. Missing-binary and
      force-off do not count as failures.
- [x] KERNEL SCAN CORRECTNESS (required for default-on): `kernel.scan` now
      returns a JSON-RPC error on a walkdir/metadata/hash IO failure instead
      of silently skipping the entry. Without this, a racy/unreadable file
      would be absent from the kernel result with `failedPaths: []`, and the
      desktop would record it as a DELETE. Erroring forces the fail-open to the
      tolerant TS scan, which reports the failed path and degrades correctly —
      preserving pre-existing reconciliation semantics. Wire protocol, method
      set, and auth model unchanged; symlink/sidecar/ignored-segment skips
      unchanged (still `continue`, not errors).

### Fail-Open Line-Level Review (Claude)

`scanWorkspaceFilesForReconcile` branches, each verified:
1. `DOHC_KERNEL_SIDECAR === "0"` -> TS, no resolution/spawn/log.
2. `workspaceKernelDisabledForProcess` (guard tripped) -> TS, no spawn/log.
3. no existing candidate binary -> TS, no spawn, NO fallback log.
4. binary exists + scan succeeds -> kernel files, `failedPaths: []`, failure
   counter reset to 0.
5. binary exists + scan/spawn throws (any class) -> increment counter, trip
   the guard at >= 3, `onError("kernel scan fallback", error)`, TS fallback.
`client.dispose()` runs in a `.catch`-guarded `finally` on every client path
(no leaked child). The only unwrapped calls are `existsSync`-based resolution
(non-throwing) and the TS fallback itself (identical to the pre-existing path).
The call site runs inside the serialized `enqueue`/`enqueueResult` chain, whose
own try/catch routes to `onError` and keeps the chain alive — a second safety
layer, so even a hypothetical propagated error cannot break capture on any
platform.

### Cross-Platform / CI-Matrix Follow-Up (NOT done here, by design)

- No cross-compilation: `build-workspace-kernel.mjs` produces the HOST binary
  only. macOS and Windows binaries come from running the same step on those
  OSes.
- Follow-up: a CI build matrix (one job per OS: linux/macOS/Windows) that runs
  the kernel build and uploads each OS's own `dohc-workspace-kernel[.exe]` into
  that OS's packaged `extraResources`, so a released app on every platform
  ships a working sidecar. Until then, platforms without a locally-built binary
  simply run the TS path (fail-open) with no user-visible impact. The kernel
  remains outside the parallel Windows validation merge bar; default-on is safe
  there precisely because a missing/broken Windows binary silently degrades.

### E2E / Visual / Manual QA

- No UI surface changed; the seam is main-process only. The default-on kernel
  path is exercised by the client suite against the real binary and by the new
  desktop unit tests; fail-open is unit-tested (missing + broken binary, both
  land reconciliation green).

### Unresolved Findings

- In un-packaged `electron-vite dev`, the repo release/debug dev path resolves
  via `repoRootFromPackage()` against the bundled main output, which may not
  land on the repo `crates/.../target` dir; dev users set
  `DOHC_KERNEL_BINARY_PATH` to engage the kernel locally. No safety/behavior
  impact on the shipped product (packaged apps resolve via
  `process.resourcesPath`; dev without a resolvable binary fails open to TS).
- Full `electron-builder package` with an empty resource dir was validated via
  package-smoke (static config gate) rather than a full package run (the
  packaging run is network-gated in this environment).
