## Y.Doc Engine Driver G2-B

Implemented milestones B1 (engine Y.Doc storage + compaction) and B2 (markdown
projection + capture integration + fidelity harness) from
`2026-07-07-think-bigger-ydoc-engine-driver-design.md`. Substrate only — NO
editor/renderer binding (the provider swap is deferred to G2-C per open
question 2). Binding decision applied: MARKDOWN-IS-THE-ARTIFACT — full Y.Doc
CRDT state is NOT persisted past a closed session, but the storage is
additive-compatible with a future persistent-threads layer.

- **Salvage.** Re-homed the proven `markdownToYDoc`/`yDocToMarkdown` roundtrip
  + `dohc-markdown-extensions` out of the hocuspocus SERVICE into a new
  framework-only package `@dohc/ydoc-projection` (tiptap + yjs only, no engine
  coupling), the shared home both the engine driver and the G2-C editor
  import. hocuspocus keeps its own copy running for live collab until the G2-C
  cutover. The copied roundtrip test passes standalone (12 tests).
- **Storage (B1).** Three lazy-additive tables in `engineDbSchema.ts`
  (`ydoc_docs` marker + head pointers, `ydoc_updates` append-only log,
  `ydoc_snapshots` compacted full state), keyed by
  `(workspace_id, version_id, object_id)`; update/snapshot bytes
  content-addressed into the existing `binary_blobs` table. A file with NO
  `ydoc_docs` row stays an ordinary text file (asserted: zero ydoc_* rows,
  unchanged read/moment behavior). Compaction (the fold the legacy stack
  skipped): fold the log into a full-state snapshot past a threshold, prune
  folded updates + superseded snapshots, byte-identical reload across the fold.
- **Projection + handoff (B2).** `createYDocEngineDriver` (new
  `ydocEngineDriver.ts`) opens a doc into a Y.Doc seeded from the current file,
  records content-addressed updates, and settles-on-quiesce via
  `store.writeTextFile` so capture records ONE ordinary moment. Single-canonical
  enforced structurally: one live session per objectId (not per version), so a
  version switch of the same object must settle+close first (never two live
  Y.Docs for one object). Close flips Y.Doc->file and prunes CRDT bytes
  (`persistClosedSessionState` flips to the additive persistent-threads path).
  Restore/external edits fold via three-way `mergeMarkdown` on the projection,
  preserving both (`.conflict`) on overlap.
- **Fidelity harness.** A corpus round-trips file->Y.Doc->file through both the
  pure projection and the driver. SURVIVES: headings, inline marks, lists,
  nesting, blockquotes, GFM tables, task lists, strikethrough, code fences, the
  custom dohc query fence, frontmatter, and Obsidian power-user syntax
  (wikilinks, embeds, tags, highlights). LOSSY (expected + pinned): Y.Doc state
  with no markdown surface — suggestion-thread / non-serialized-mark sidecars —
  is dropped on every close (a future persistent-threads layer, not the .md
  file, is what would preserve it).

### Gate fix round (G2-B adversarial review)

Adversarial review + CodeRabbit found substrate-correctness gaps; all fixed
tests-first:

- **[HIGH] Single-canonical was per-instance.** The live-session registry was a
  per-`createYDocEngineDriver()` map, so two drivers on the same engine.db could
  both open one object (even different versions). Moved the reservation to a
  PROCESS-GLOBAL set keyed by normalized engine-db path + workspace + object,
  re-checked/reserved before any open/reset. Test: two separate driver instances
  (separate stores) on one rootDir — the second open (same and different version)
  throws `already-live`.
- **[HIGH] Second-connection two-writer deadlock.** `recordUpdate` used a second
  in-process SQLite connection + `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` while settle wrote through the
  store connection — node:sqlite busy-waits block the JS thread, so concurrent
  settle + append could deadlock. Added `VersionedTextStore.runInEngineWriteLane`
  (serialized queue + store connection + one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) and routed ALL
  driver writes (blob puts, update/snapshot rows, head pointers, reset, prune,
  compact) through it. The driver keeps its own connection for READS only. Test:
  40 appends racing settles complete without hanging, head monotonic to 40.
- **[MED] `loadPersistedDoc` returned a blank doc after prune.** A default close
  prunes snapshots/updates but keeps the marker; `loadPersistedDoc` handed back
  an empty Y.Doc. Now returns `null` (seed-from-file) when a marker has no
  persisted state. Test: after close, `isYDocDriven` true but `loadPersistedDoc`
  is `null`.
- **[MED] "replicates for free" was false + GC-root gap.** ydoc_* blobs are
  LOCAL-ONLY (no replication op references them) until G2-C. Corrected the
  claims (driver header, schema comment, this log) and documented the GC-root
  invariant: a blob referenced by a live `ydoc_updates`/`ydoc_snapshots` head is
  NOT collectable (coordinate with the parallel sync-hardening blob GC).
- **[LOW] Unverified blob read.** `readYDocBlob` now verifies
  `sha256(content) === sha` and byte_length, matching the relay/blob posture.
  Test: a tampered blob row (matching length, wrong bytes) is rejected on read.
- **[CR major] ON DELETE CASCADE.** `ydoc_docs` now FK-cascades from
  `file_objects`, and `ydoc_updates`/`ydoc_snapshots` cascade through
  `ydoc_docs`, so deleting a rich-doc file leaves no orphaned ydoc_* rows.
  (`resetPersistedState` reordered to upsert the marker before the base snapshot
  so the new child FK is satisfied.)
- **[CR major] Code-fence fidelity.** The `DohcQueryBlock` `parseMarkdown` DEFERS
  a non-query fence (returns the empty `MarkdownParseResult` — the type-valid
  defer signal in @tiptap/markdown; `null` is not permitted) so ordinary code
  blocks fall through to the default handler instead of being dropped. Test:
  plain ` ```js ` / no-language fences round-trip; a `query` fence still becomes
  a query block.

## Sync Hardening (0P follow-ups)

Closes the four "carried unsolved" robustness items from the Arc 0P sync work.
All four are correctness-critical for multi-machine data integrity. Landed
tests-first, platform-neutral (Linux-verified). Commits: items 1+2 (engine),
item 4 (relay), item 3 (engine + desktop).

### Item 1 — deterministic conflict-id symmetry

Sync divergence conflicts are minted independently on each machine (they never
replicate as `conflict.open` ops), so the old id embedded the local head +
incoming moment id and differed per side, forcing the resolve path onto a
fragile swapped-head lookup. Now a sync conflict's id is a pure function of
`(workspaceId, versionId, objectId, fork-point moment)` — the fork point being
`beforeLatestMomentId` of the first divergent op, which per-origin FIFO makes
identical on both machines. Both sides therefore compute the SAME id, and
`conflict.resolve` closes the peer's mirror BY ID: the resolve path looks up the
local row by the payload's conflictId first, routing sync conflicts (origin
`sync`, current/incoming swapped) through the mirror-flip + state adoption and
merge conflicts (replicated verbatim via `conflict.open`) through a plain
update. The existing swapped-head lookup remains as the fallback ONLY when ids
genuinely cannot align — occupancy conflicts (inherently asymmetric) and
pre-deterministic rows.

### Item 2 — conflict coalescing

`openOrCoalesceSyncConflict` keeps one OPEN sync conflict per (version, object)
lineage: a newer divergent remote op updates the existing open row's incoming
head + updatedAtMs instead of stacking a second row. The current side is left
as first recorded (this machine's own head; local writes advance the file
independently, and resolve always re-reads the live head before acting, so a
lagging current is never acted on stale). Interacts with item 1: the deterministic
id is minted once at first divergence and never re-derived, so coalescing keeps
one stable identity across an episode.

### Item 3 — origin-reset recovery preserving unpushed work

`recoverRelayOrigin` turns the previously dead-end `RelayOriginDivergedError`
(restored-from-older / cloned engine.db) into a recovery: it computes the
byte-identical shared history prefix against the relay's authoritative record
for the origin, re-journals the divergent tail ("orphans") under a FRESH origin
id (so they push cleanly), drops the orphan rows from the old origin (so the
relay's authoritative versions apply as REMOTE ops — opening ordinary conflicts
where they clash instead of being idempotently skipped), marks the old origin
fully pushed, and resets the fetch cursor. Genuinely-unpushed local work is
never dropped — it is preserved as pushed-under-a-new-origin content and, where
it clashes, as an open conflict on both machines. The desktop relay sync loop
catches the diverged error, recovers, and re-pushes so the pass completes.

### Item 4 — relay GC / quotas

(a) A per-workspace storage quota (`SYNC_RELAY_WORKSPACE_QUOTA_BYTES`, default
2 GiB) enforced inside the same transaction as blob-put and log-append; a new
blob or a log batch that would exceed the workspace's total (blobs + log
payloads) is rejected with `SyncRelayQuotaExceededError` (413, `quota_exceeded`).
Idempotent re-PUTs add no bytes; over-quota log appends roll back atomically.
(b) `collectUnreferencedBlobs`, behind an owner-only `POST /sync/:ws/maintenance/gc`,
removes only blobs no live log row references (orphaned uploads from a push that
failed before its log append). GC only ever DELETEs from `sync_relay_blobs` —
the append-only log and the key-envelope history are never pruned.

## Agent Notifications and Mentions

LOCAL, individual-first: the single user + their own agents. No relay/cloud
replication, presence, DMs, or shared channels (those stay behind the
collaboration flag). Everything here is derived from the in-process agent
session and the engine chat store already on this machine.

### Notification model (pure: `agentNotifications.ts`)

- Triggers, one per run: `finished` (status → completed), `needs-input`
  (status → waiting-permission, i.e. blocked on an approval/question),
  `asked` (a completion whose latest agent message @mentions the user or ends
  in a question), `error` (status → failed). Priority error > needs-input >
  asked > finished.
- Coalescing: notices key on `${workspaceId}::${runId}::${kind}`. Repeated
  polls of the same state never duplicate or re-stamp; a transition to a new
  kind supersedes the old kind's notice for that run; other runs/workspaces
  are untouched.
- Auto-clear: a run that resumes (desired kind → null) drops its notice; a
  `dismissed` key set suppresses re-raising a state the user already saw;
  `clearAgentNotificationsForWorkspace` (opening the Agent panel) and
  `clearAgentNotificationsForThread` (opening the chat) are the open-side
  auto-clears. `deriveAgentActivity` folds a session snapshot into the flat
  input (latest-assistant summary + addressed-to-user detection).
- `useAgentNotifications` polls `getAgentSessionState` for the active
  workspace (1.5s) so a background run finishing off-screen still surfaces.
  Scope: the currently open workspace only — cross-workspace polling is the
  one obvious future addition (and the seam multi-user lanes will also want).

### Mentions (pure: `mentions.ts`)

- Parser resolves `@handle` against a candidate roster (the user + agents),
  email-safe boundary handling, unknown handles stay plain text. Segments for
  chip rendering; `mentionsAnyCandidate` for addressed-to-user.
- Autocomplete: `activeMentionQuery` (caret token), `matchMentionCandidates`
  (prefix/substring ranking, agent-first on ties), `applyMentionCompletion`.
- `MentionComposer` wires it into the composer: while the menu is open
  Enter/Tab accept the highlight (never send); Enter sends when closed;
  IME-safe. combobox/listbox roles + aria-activedescendant.
- User → agent invoke: a sent message that @mentions an agent calls the
  shell's `handleAgentMentioned`, which starts an agent session prompting it
  to `dohc_read_chat` + `dohc_reply_to_chat` in that thread (the existing
  two-way agent-chat reply path). Guarded when an agent is already busy.

### Surfaces

- NoticeCenter renders agent notices (newest first) with Open + dismiss.
- `MentionText` chips in the shared `ChatMessageList` (both the workspace
  Chats view and the file rail can opt in via `mentionCandidates`).
- "Addressed to me" inbox: a calm section atop ChatsView listing asks /
  needs-input, hidden when empty — reuses the notification model, no new
  backend query.

### UI copy inventory

- finished — "Your agent finished" / summary or "Your agent wrapped up its
  work in <workspace>."
- needs-input — "Your agent needs you" / "Waiting for your go-ahead: <perm>"
- asked — "Your agent has a question" / summary or "Your agent asked you
  something in <workspace>."
- error — "Your agent hit a problem" / the failure reason.
- Composer placeholder gains "  @ to mention"; inbox header "Addressed to me";
  busy-invoke note "Your agent is busy right now — it'll pick up the mention
  on its next turn."; no-driver note "No agent is set up to mention yet —
  connect one in the Agent panel."

### Shared-code note (multi-user lanes)

`mentions.ts` is deliberately free of desktop-only imports so member/agent
handle resolution can move to a shared package when the collaboration lanes
land; the notification model's coalescing/dismissal keying is per-run and
reusable for teammate-authored asks too.

## Y.Doc Replication G2-C-1

Makes engine-native Y.Doc rich-doc state (the G2-B substrate) REPLICATE across
machines over the sync relay: the `ydoc.update` op kind, its commutative CRDT
apply, driver journaling, blob transport, and GC-root wiring. Substrate +
replication only — NO editor/renderer binding (G2-C-2), NO Hocuspocus deletion
(G2-C-3). Tests-first, Linux-verified. Basis:
`2026-07-07-think-bigger-ydoc-engine-driver-design.md` §G2-C1.

### The `ydoc.update` op design

- **Payload** (`YDocUpdatePayload`, contracts): `versionId`, `objectId`, `path`
  (projection target + secret-floor gate), `contentKind` (`richdoc`/`plaintext`),
  `updateBlobSha256` (the Yjs update bytes, content-addressed into
  `binary_blobs`), and `isBaseState?`. Carried in the standard envelope with
  `(originId, originSeq, recordedAtMs)` like every op.
- **Snapshot strategy: reuse the update stream, no separate op kind.** A
  ydoc.update is any `Y.applyUpdate`-able byte string. The driver emits ONE
  full-state BASE op (`isBaseState`, `Y.encodeStateAsUpdate(seed)`) when a live
  session's replication baseline is established (open / merge-reseed), then
  DELTA ops per edit. The base op makes the stream self-contained (a from-
  scratch peer with no file reconstructs the doc) and re-bases replay each open;
  peer-side compaction (threshold 128) folds the log into a fresh snapshot to
  bound replay.

### The commutative apply (how it differs from P0D, why convergence holds)

`moment.append` carries `before_latest_moment_id` and takes the head-check /
divergence path (fast-forward or open a P0D conflict). `ydoc.update` is
different in kind: Yjs updates are **commutative CRDT deltas**, so the apply
branch (`versionedTextStore.applyReplicationOp`) does NO head check, opens NO
conflict row, and has NO `before` guard. It: (1) digest-verifies the hydrated
update blob, (2) reconstructs the converged Y.Doc in memory (existing persisted
state + `Y.applyUpdate` of the new update), (3) re-projects markdown and
materializes it as a LOCAL, NON-JOURNALING settle (`writeProjectedTextFile` /
`suppressReplicationJournal`), (4) persists the CRDT rows (append + advance
head, pinning the ORIGIN's `objectId` so the file and the `ydoc_docs` marker
share cross-machine identity). Convergence is guaranteed by Yjs semantics, not
the log: any arrival order converges, a re-applied update is a Yjs no-op, and
the log's per-origin `acked_seq` dedup makes re-import a no-op at the log level
too (CRDT idempotence is the backstop). A live co-edit therefore produces ONLY
fine-grained ydoc.update ops — the settle NEVER journals moment.append, so two
peers' independent settles can never collide into a P0D conflict on markdown the
CRDT already reconciled (this is the single-replication-channel invariant).

### Blob-upload-before-log ordering

`collectBlobHashesFromOp` (engine) and `referencedBlobShas` (relay) now count a
ydoc.update's `updateBlobSha256` as a binary blob. The existing push path
(`uploadMissingBlobs` before `appendOriginOps`) therefore ships the update blob
BEFORE the log op, and the relay's append-time blob-ref validation is satisfied.
The driver journals the ydoc.update op in the SAME write-lane transaction as the
`ydoc_updates` append, so the blob is already in `binary_blobs` when the op is
appended locally.

### GC-root wiring

`referencedBlobShas` counting the update blob makes a blob referenced by a live
ydoc.update log op a relay GC ROOT — `collectUnreferencedBlobs` never reclaims
it (proven: survives GC with a zero grace window while a sibling orphan is
collected). Engine-side, the G2-B invariant holds unchanged (a blob referenced
by a live `ydoc_updates`/`ydoc_snapshots` head is a root; the pull path adds the
projected path to `candidateMaterializationPaths` so the on-disk file settles).

### Secret floor

The apply rejects a ydoc.update whose `path` classifies as `secret`
(`.env` family) BEFORE any materialization — no `ydoc_docs` marker, no file, no
plaintext-leak path for secret files. Defense in depth: the driver's
`openSession` independently rejects secret-classified paths, so a secret file
can never be opened as a live Y.Doc either. Both proven by test.

### G2-C-2 / G2-C-3 handoff

- **G2-C-2 (editor provider).** Replace the renderer `HocuspocusProvider`
  (`useCollabDoc.ts`) with an engine provider driving
  `driver.openSession`/`recordUpdate`/`settle`/`close`. Two invariants this lane
  established that the provider MUST honor: (a) **join-before-edit** — a peer
  must apply the doc's replicated lineage and open with `resume: true` (seed from
  `loadPersistedDoc`, NOT re-seed from the file) before editing; two independent
  `markdownToYDoc` seeds of the same file mint different Yjs item ids and merging
  them DUPLICATES content (inherent CRDT property). (b) The provider must apply
  incoming remote ydoc.update deltas into the LIVE Y.Doc (this lane converges
  PERSISTED state; the live in-memory doc is the provider's responsibility).
  Awareness (presence/cursors) is ephemeral and MUST NOT journal — a separate
  non-durable channel (still G2-C-2).
- **G2-C-3 (Hocuspocus retirement).** Delete `services/hocuspocus`, the
  collab-token route + IPC, and the hocuspocus provider; cut over at a closed-
  session boundary. Replication is now engine-native, so nothing in the relay
  path depends on Hocuspocus.

## Y.Doc Replication G2-C-1 — gate fix round (durable-resume lifecycle)

An adversarial review found 3 HIGH + 1 MEDIUM convergence/data-integrity bugs in
the first cut. The root cause of the two most severe was that a REPLICATED doc
was NOT treated as one durable lineage: it pruned its CRDT on close and re-seeded
from markdown on reopen, minting a second independent base op — and a fresh peer
replaying `base1 + deltas + base2` merged two lineages into DUPLICATED content.
Fixed tests-first (each HIGH gets a test that reproduces the divergence/loss).

### The unifying principle — durable-resume vs local-only prune

A doc that participates in replication is now ONE durable CRDT lineage
(`createYDocEngineDriver({ replicated: true })`):

- **First creation** (no persisted lineage): seed from the file's markdown and
  emit the full-state BASE `ydoc.update` op EXACTLY ONCE.
- **Every subsequent open**: ALWAYS resume from the persisted/replicated CRDT
  (`loadPersistedDoc`) — the `resume` flag is forced on for a replicated doc, so
  a caller can no longer accidentally re-seed. A re-seed forks a second lineage
  (a fresh `markdownToYDoc` mints new Yjs ids) and duplicates on replay.
- **Close**: settle the projection but NEVER prune the CRDT rows — they stay
  durable for the next resume AND for a peer bootstrapping from the log. A
  replicated doc therefore emits a base ONCE and never prunes.

Prune-on-close (and reseed-on-open, and NO `ydoc.update` journaling at all) stays
ONLY for `replicated: false` LOCAL-ONLY docs — markdown-is-the-artifact for the
solo case. A doc that never replicated cannot diverge a peer, so pruning it is
safe. `persistClosedSessionState` still keeps even a local-only doc's CRDT durable
(future persistent-threads layer). The split is documented in the LIFECYCLE
SPLIT header of `ydocEngineDriver.ts`.

### The four fixes

1. **[HIGH] Repeated independent BASE ops diverge/duplicate** — durable-resume as
   above. A replicated doc journals its base ONCE (`resetPersistedState` runs only
   on first creation), always resumes, and `close` compacts-not-prunes. TEST:
   `close→reopen(no resume flag)→edit` on A, a fresh peer B replays the full log →
   byte-identical state + markdown, each line present exactly once, `baseOpCount`
   is 1; plus a seeded close/reopen fuzz. Extended the real relay child-process
   test to cover the reopen-then-fresh-peer bootstrap (base-once over HTTP).
2. **[HIGH] objectId pinning bypassed on the occupied path** — `projectYDocUpdate`
   now REJECTS a ydoc.update before materializing when any snapshot at
   `payload.path` is a DIFFERENT object, or any snapshot for `payload.objectId`
   sits at a different path (no Y.Doc rename protocol). Stops object A's op from
   writing through object B's occupied path. TEST: a ydoc.update for object A
   carrying B's path is rejected; B's file untouched, no marker minted.
3. **[HIGH] Remote update not applied to the live in-memory doc → loss on close**
   — a process-global live-doc registry (`liveYDocRegistry.ts`, keyed exactly like
   the driver's single-canonical reservation). The driver registers a replicated
   session's live Y.Doc on open and unregisters on close; `applyReplicationOp`
   routes an applied remote `ydoc.update` straight into that live doc with
   `Y.applyUpdate`, so the eventual close settles the CONVERGED state, never a
   stale one over newer CRDT. TEST: object live in a session, a remote update
   arrives, the session makes a local edit and closes → the remote edit is in the
   final projection file + persisted state (dropped without the routing).
4. **[MEDIUM] Uncapped local update size** — `recordUpdate` rejects an update over
   `MAX_VERSIONED_BINARY_FILE_BYTES` (5 MiB) BEFORE the blob put + journal, so an
   oversized update that every peer would reject on hydrate is never stored or
   pushed. TEST: a ~6 MiB update is rejected; no `ydoc_updates` row, no journaled op.

- `pnpm -r typecheck` clean repo-wide.
- workspace-engine 442 (was 437: +5 `ydocReplication.test.ts` — close/reopen
  convergence base-once, close/reopen fuzz, objectId/path rejection, live-session
  apply survival, oversized-update rejection) + changeSetStore 39/5-skip green.
  Both HIGH tests verified load-bearing (red with the fix reverted).

  close→reopen→edit cycle + base-once + no-duplication assertions).

### G2-C-2 handoff update (durable-resume — the editor provider MUST resume)

The engine provider replacing `HocuspocusProvider` MUST drive the driver with
`replicated: true` and MUST NOT re-seed a replicated doc: opening now ALWAYS
resumes an existing lineage (the `resume` flag is forced on internally), so the
provider just calls `driver.openSession` — never a fresh `markdownToYDoc` seed
for a doc that already has a lineage. Incoming remote `ydoc.update` deltas are
already routed into the LIVE Y.Doc by the engine (fix 3), so the provider does
not have to reconcile persisted-vs-live itself; it binds the editor to
`session.doc` and lets `recordUpdate` journal local edits. Awareness
(presence/cursors) is still ephemeral and MUST NOT journal.

## Y.Doc Editor Binding G2-C-2

Lane G2-C-2: bind the desktop rich-text editor to the engine-native Y.Doc,
replacing HocuspocusProvider, so solo editing runs on the engine Y.Doc and
co-editing rides the G2-C-1 replication. Design doc:
`2026-07-07-think-bigger-ydoc-engine-driver-design.md` §G2-C2 + the durable-
resume handoff notes.

### The provider design (bind / observe / skip-reserved-origin / settle / close)

The engine driver is node-only (node:sqlite + the store write lane), so the
live `session.doc` lives in MAIN and the renderer's Tiptap editor binds to a
MIRROR doc kept convergent over IPC. The provider is therefore TWO halves:

- **Main core** — `apps/desktop/src/collab/ydocEngineProviderSession.ts`
  (`openEngineYDocProviderSession`). Constructs the driver with
  `replicated: true` (contract a — openSession resumes the lineage internally;
  the core NEVER re-seeds), binds to `session.doc`, and installs ONE
  `doc.on("update", (u, origin) => …)` observer:
  - `origin === REMOTE_YDOC_APPLY_ORIGIN` → forward to the editor via
    `onRemoteUpdate`, **never** `recordUpdate` (contract b — the store already
    persisted+journaled+acked that remote op; re-journaling echo-storms peers);
    schedule a settle so the converged state projects.
  - `origin === LOCAL_EDITOR_ORIGIN` (stamped by `applyLocalUpdate`) → journal
    via `session.recordUpdate` (persists the CRDT delta AND the replicated
    `ydoc.update` op) and schedule a debounced settle.
  - any other origin → ignored.
  `applyLocalUpdate` = `Y.applyUpdate(session.doc, u, LOCAL_EDITOR_ORIGIN)`.
  Journaling is serialized (promise chain) to keep `ydoc_updates.seq` in
  emission order; settle is debounced (800ms, matching the local autosave feel)
  and coalesced. `close()` drains pending journal+settle, settles the converged
  state, then releases the single-canonical reservation (`session.close`) and
  the driver read handle — so a version switch of the same object can reopen.
  `applyExternalMarkdownEdit` swallows the replicated `invalid-input` rejection
  and returns `{ supported: false }` (contract c — external-edit-as-deltas is
  G2-C-3/later; the live session must not crash on an agent/restore write).
- **Renderer half** — `apps/desktop/src/renderer/collab/engineYDocProvider.ts`
  (`bindEngineYDoc(transport)`). The drop-in replacement for HocuspocusProvider:
  seeds a mirror `Y.Doc` from the engine's `initialUpdate` under a private
  `ENGINE_SOURCED_ORIGIN`, ships every non-engine-origin (real editor) update to
  main via the transport, and applies forwarded remote deltas under the engine
  origin so they render live but never echo back to main. Exposes `doc` for the
  Tiptap Collaboration extension (`field: "body"`), `available`, and an
  idempotent `destroy()`. No websocket, no token, no `collabToken`.

### How the three G2-C-1 contracts are honored (proven in tests)

- (a) replicated:true + never-reseed: the core only constructs
  `{ replicated: true }` and binds `session.doc`; the driver's openSession
  resumes. Proven by the close→reopen round-trip test (the earlier edit
  survives via the CRDT lineage, not a fresh markdown seed).
- (b) skip `REMOTE_YDOC_APPLY_ORIGIN`: the "no echo storm" test routes a remote
  delta into `session.doc` under the reserved origin and asserts it is
  **forwarded** (onRemoteUpdate fires) but produces **no new `ydoc_updates`
  row**, while still converging (a following settle projects the remote line).
- (c) graceful external edit: `applyExternalMarkdownEdit` on a replicated doc
  returns `{ supported: false }` and the session stays alive+editable.

### Solo-editing-on-engine proof (no relay, no cloud)

`ydocEngineProviderSession.test.ts` (real store + real Yjs, no Electron): open a
plain local rich file → a mirror-bridged editor edit journals through
`recordUpdate` → `settleNow` projects it into `engine.db` AND hands markdown to
`onSettled` for the disk write → close → reopen resumes the rich content. Same
provider drives co-editing: a remote `ydoc.update` the engine routes into
`session.doc` (liveYDocRegistry) is forwarded to the editor unchanged.

### Verification (Linux-green)

- `ydocEngineProviderSession.test.ts` — 6 tests (solo settle round-trip,
  reserved-origin skip, close/reopen resume, single-canonical version-switch
  handoff, graceful external-edit, secret-path refusal).
- `engineYDocProvider.test.ts` — 4 tests (seed, ship-local + receive-remote
  without echo, unavailable fallback, idempotent destroy).
- `pnpm --filter @dohc/desktop typecheck` green.

### What is BUILT vs. what remains (honest scope)

BUILT + tested + committed: both provider halves — the contract heart of "the
editor binds to the engine Y.Doc, not Hocuspocus". These are the reusable,
transport-agnostic pieces; the main core is what the IPC layer wraps, the
renderer half is what `useCollabDoc`'s sibling hook drives.

REMAINING (a runtime-sensitive integration on the editor's riskiest path +
the security-reviewed capture module — handed off, NOT landed blind):

1. **Share the capture's store with the YDoc session.** The YDoc driver needs
   the SAME `VersionedTextStore` instance the desktop capture owns (single-
   writer safety: two stores on one `engine.db` = two write connections =
   node:sqlite deadlock). `WorkspaceEngineCapture` does not expose its store or
   active version yet — add an accessor (e.g. `engineStore()` +
   `activeVersionId()`), or an `openYDocSession(path)` method on the capture
   that constructs `openEngineYDocProviderSession({ store, rootDir, versionId })`
   with its own store.
2. **Capture-watcher coexistence.** A live ydoc-driven path's settle writes the
   disk `.md`; the capture watcher would re-capture it as a `moment.append` (and
   for a SHARED workspace, double-replicate → P0D conflict on the markdown the
   `ydoc.update` stream already reconciles). Teach the capture to defer for a
   live ydoc path: consult `driver.canonicalSourceFor`/`isYDocDriven` and
   suppress `moment.append` (use `writeProjectedTextFile`, or recognize the
   settle's self-write sha) while a session is live. For SOLO/local this is
   benign today (no relay), so a solo-first cutover can land ahead of the shared
   coexistence hardening.
3. **IPC surface.** Channels `engineYDocOpen` / `engineYDocApplyUpdate` /
   `engineYDocClose` + a `engineYDocRemoteUpdate` main→renderer event (mirror the
   `searchWorkspace`/`onSearchResults` streaming pattern: Zod payloads in
   channels.ts, handlers in main.ts gated on `activity.engineCaptureFor`,
   preload subscription, bridge-contract types). Updates cross IPC as
   `Uint8Array` (structured clone). Gate open on engine-flagged workspace + a
   rich/markdown path; catch the driver's secret/not-found/already-live throws
   and return `{ available: false }`.
4. **Renderer transport + hook + FileInspector flip.** An `EngineYDocTransport`
   implementation over the bridge, a `useEngineDoc` hook (sibling to
   `useCollabDoc`) that `bindEngineYDoc`s it, and switching `FileInspector`'s
   editor to it for local rich docs — keeping the save-state/Edit-gate UX for
   solo (the collab branch currently drops `markdown-save-state`; solo-on-engine
   should keep a settle indicator so the editing feel is unchanged). Undo/redo:
   `COLLAB_STARTER_KIT` already disables `undoRedo`; the Collaboration extension
   must supply the Yjs `UndoManager` binding so undo stays intact.
5. **e2e.** Adjust `workspace-collab-decoupling.spec.ts` — local editing now
   flows THROUGH the engine provider (still zero WebSocket, `collabToken` still
   `{ available: false }`) — and add an editor-on-engine round-trip spec
   (type → settle → reopen through `engine.db` + the `.md`).

### G2-C-3 handoff (what is now safe to delete)

Once the FileInspector flip (item 4) lands, the editor no longer instantiates
`HocuspocusProvider`. G2-C-3 can then delete: the Hocuspocus service
(`services/hocuspocus`), the `collab-token` route + the `collabToken` IPC +
`deriveHocuspocusUrl`, and the `HocuspocusProvider` code path in
`useCollabDoc.ts`/`collabSession.ts`. The cloud co-editing cutover the user
chose: a shared workspace now co-edits through the engine provider (the same
`ydoc.update` replication), not Hocuspocus — ship the closed-boundary migration
tool (file == re-projection, else preserve-both) as part of the retirement.

### MU-C1 handoff (presence)

The provider exposes the live `session.doc`; MU-C1 presence can bind Yjs
awareness to it as the ephemeral channel (never journaled), replacing the
Hocuspocus awareness the old `useCollabDoc` used. Awareness updates must NOT go
through `recordUpdate` (they are not `ydoc.update` ops).
